questions.text: The 1969 Woodstock festival was held on a dairy farm in which New York town?
questions.fun_fact: The site, Max Yasgur's farm, lies about 95 km southwest of the town of Woodstock itself.

questions.text: Which country won the 2010 FIFA World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: Spain became the first team to win the World Cup after losing its opening game, 1–0 to Switzerland.

questions.text: Which country hosted the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.fun_fact: Only 13 teams took part, and the hosts beat Argentina 4–2 in the final in Montevideo.

questions.text: Which player scored the 'Hand of God' goal at the 1986 FIFA World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: Four minutes later, in the same quarter-final against England, he scored the dribble later voted 'Goal of the Century'.

questions.text: Which country co-hosted the 2002 FIFA World Cup with Japan?
questions.fun_fact: It was the first World Cup played in Asia and the first shared by two host nations.

questions.text: How many players does each team have on the field at the start of a standard soccer match?
questions.fun_fact: If a team is reduced to fewer than seven players, the match should not continue.

questions.text: What color card does a soccer referee show to send a player off?
questions.fun_fact: Penalty cards were first used at the 1970 World Cup, based on referee Ken Aston's traffic-light idea.

questions.text: Which country won UEFA Euro 2004?
questions.fun_fact: Greece beat hosts Portugal twice: in the tournament's opening match and again in the final.

questions.text: Which country won UEFA Euro 1992?
questions.fun_fact: Denmark had not even qualified; they took Yugoslavia's place after it was excluded shortly before the tournament.

questions.text: Which country won the first FIFA Women's World Cup in 1991?
questions.fun_fact: The tournament was held in China, and its matches lasted 80 minutes instead of the usual 90.

questions.text: Which country won its first Copa América title in 2015?
questions.fun_fact: Chile beat Argentina on penalties in the final, then did exactly the same in the 2016 Copa América Centenario final.

questions.text: Which country won the 1954 FIFA World Cup final, remembered as the 'Miracle of Bern'?
questions.fun_fact: Hungary had beaten West Germany 8–3 in the group stage of the same tournament.

questions.text: Which country hosted the 1958 FIFA World Cup, where a 17-year-old Pelé starred?
questions.fun_fact: Brazil beat the hosts 5–2 in the final at the Råsunda Stadium in Solna.

questions.text: Which country won the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations, held in Egypt?
questions.fun_fact: Algeria beat Senegal 1–0 in the final for their second title, and their first since 1990.

questions.text: Which country won the 2019 AFC Asian Cup, held in the United Arab Emirates?
questions.fun_fact: Qatar beat four-time champions Japan 3–1 in the final in Abu Dhabi.

questions.text: Which club became the first British winner of the European Cup, in 1967?
questions.fun_fact: The side was nicknamed the 'Lisbon Lions' after beating Inter Milan 2–1 in the final near Lisbon.

questions.text: How wide is a standard soccer goal, measured between the inside of the posts?
questions.fun_fact: The underside of the crossbar must be 2.44 m (8 ft) above the ground.

questions.text: In American football, how many points is a touchdown worth?
questions.fun_fact: After a touchdown, the scoring team can try for one extra point with a kick or two points with a play from scrimmage.

questions.text: Which city hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics?
questions.fun_fact: They were the first Olympic Games ever held in South America.

questions.text: In which city did Jesse Owens win four Olympic gold medals in 1936?
questions.fun_fact: His four golds came in the 100 m, 200 m, long jump and 4 × 100 m relay.

questions.text: How many interlocking rings appear on the Olympic flag?
questions.fun_fact: The rings were designed in 1913, and the flag was first flown at an Olympic Games in Antwerp in 1920.

questions.text: Which city hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics?
questions.fun_fact: Cathy Freeman lit the Olympic cauldron at the opening ceremony and later won the 400 m gold.

questions.text: Which town hosted the first Winter Olympics in 1924?
questions.fun_fact: It was staged as an 'International Winter Sports Week' and only recognized as the first Winter Olympics afterward.

questions.text: At which Olympic Games did breaking (breakdancing) make its debut?
questions.fun_fact: Breaking had already been tested at the 2018 Youth Olympic Games in Buenos Aires.

questions.text: Which city hosted the 1972 Winter Olympics, the first held outside Europe and North America?
questions.fun_fact: Sapporo had first been awarded the 1940 Winter Games, which were never held.

questions.text: Which martial art made its Olympic debut at Tokyo 2020 but was left out of Paris 2024?
questions.fun_fact: Medals were awarded in two disciplines: kata, a solo display of forms, and kumite, which is sparring.

questions.text: Who scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics, in 1976?
questions.fun_fact: The scoreboard displayed 1.00, because it had not been built to show a score of 10.

questions.text: At which Summer Olympics was tug of war last contested as an Olympic event?
questions.fun_fact: At London 1908, all three tug of war medals went to British police teams.

questions.text: At which Olympic Games did beach volleyball become a full medal sport?
questions.fun_fact: Brazil's Jackie Silva and Sandra Pires won the first Olympic women's beach volleyball gold.

questions.text: The modern pentathlon was first held at which Olympic Games?
questions.fun_fact: It was a men-only Olympic event until a women's competition was added at Sydney 2000.

questions.text: At which Olympic Games did Finland's Paavo Nurmi win five gold medals?
questions.fun_fact: He won the 1,500 m and 5,000 m finals on the same day, with less than two hours between the two races.

questions.text: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is played on clay courts?
questions.fun_fact: Its venue, Stade Roland Garros, is named after a pioneering French aviator.

questions.text: On which surface is the Wimbledon tennis tournament played?
questions.fun_fact: Wimbledon's dress code requires players to wear almost entirely white clothing.

questions.text: In tennis, what is a score of 40–40 in a game called?
questions.fun_fact: Under 'no-ad' scoring, used in some events, the next point after deuce simply wins the game.

questions.text: Who won the 2008 Wimbledon men's singles final against Roger Federer?
questions.fun_fact: Delayed by rain, the final ended in near darkness after 4 hours 48 minutes of play.

questions.text: Which player won all four tennis majors and Olympic gold in 1988, the 'Golden Slam'?
questions.fun_fact: Four years earlier, aged 15, she had won the tennis demonstration event at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.

questions.text: Who in 1975 became the first Black man to win the Wimbledon singles title?
questions.fun_fact: In the final he beat the defending champion, Jimmy Connors.

questions.text: Which nation won the very first Davis Cup in 1900?
questions.fun_fact: Dwight Davis, who donated the trophy, also played for the winning US team.

questions.text: At which Grand Slam did Li Na become the first Chinese player to win a singles major, in 2011?
questions.fun_fact: She won a second major at the 2014 Australian Open.

questions.text: In modern cricket, how many legal deliveries make up an over?
questions.fun_fact: Test matches in Australia used eight-ball overs until the late 1970s.

questions.text: What is the name of the famous Test cricket series between England and Australia?
questions.fun_fact: The tiny urn at the heart of the rivalry is believed to hold the ashes of a burnt cricket bail.

questions.text: In cricket, what is a batter's score of zero called?
questions.fun_fact: Being dismissed for zero on the very first ball faced is called a 'golden duck'.

questions.text: Which team won the first Cricket World Cup in 1975?
questions.fun_fact: Captain Clive Lloyd scored a century in the final against Australia at Lord's.

questions.text: Which country won the 1983 Cricket World Cup by beating the West Indies in the final?
questions.fun_fact: India defended a total of just 183 runs, bowling the West Indies out for 140.

questions.text: How long is a cricket pitch from one set of stumps to the other?
questions.fun_fact: 22 yards is exactly one chain, an old English unit used for measuring land.

questions.text: In which sport was the term 'hat-trick' first used?
questions.fun_fact: In 1858, H. H. Stephenson took three wickets with three balls and was given a hat bought with a collection.

questions.text: Which country won the 1996 Cricket World Cup final in Lahore?
questions.fun_fact: Aravinda de Silva hit an unbeaten century as Sri Lanka chased down Australia's total.

questions.text: How many players does a rugby union team have on the field?
questions.fun_fact: Rugby league sides field 13 players, while rugby sevens uses just seven per team.

questions.text: Which national rugby team is famous for performing the haka 'Ka Mate' before matches?
questions.fun_fact: Ka Mate was composed around 1820 by the Māori chief Te Rauparaha.

questions.text: Which country won the first Rugby World Cup in 1987?
questions.fun_fact: The first tournament was co-hosted by New Zealand and Australia.

questions.text: Which country joined in 2000, turning rugby's Five Nations into the Six Nations?
questions.fun_fact: Italy won its first Six Nations match, beating defending champions Scotland in Rome.

questions.text: According to legend, which Rugby School pupil first picked up the ball and ran with it in 1823?
questions.fun_fact: The Rugby World Cup trophy is named the Webb Ellis Cup in his honor.

questions.text: Which country hosted the 2019 Rugby World Cup, the first held in Asia?
questions.fun_fact: The hosts beat Ireland and Scotland to reach the quarter-finals for the first time.

questions.text: In NBA basketball, how many points is a field goal from beyond the arc worth?
questions.fun_fact: The NBA adopted the three-point line for the 1979–80 season.

questions.text: Who invented basketball in 1891?
questions.fun_fact: The first game was played with a soccer ball and two peach baskets as goals.

questions.text: In which city did the US 'Dream Team' win Olympic basketball gold in 1992?
questions.fun_fact: It was the first Olympics at which active NBA players were allowed to compete.

questions.text: Which country won the 2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup, held in China?
questions.fun_fact: Spain beat Argentina 95–75 in the final in Beijing.

questions.text: Which Italian Formula One circuit is nicknamed the 'Temple of Speed'?
questions.fun_fact: Its steeply banked oval section was used for the Italian Grand Prix until 1961.

questions.text: Which country hosted Formula One's first night race in 2008?
questions.fun_fact: Abu Dhabi followed in 2009 with a race that started in daylight and finished under floodlights.

questions.text: Which team won 15 of the 16 Formula One races in 1988?
questions.fun_fact: The only race McLaren lost that year was at Monza, won by Ferrari's Gerhard Berger.

questions.text: In which city is the Interlagos Formula One circuit located?
questions.fun_fact: Its official name honors José Carlos Pace, a Brazilian Formula One driver.

questions.text: Who won the first Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 1950?
questions.fun_fact: The first championship race was the 1950 British Grand Prix at Silverstone.

questions.text: Who won the 2007 Formula One World Championship by a single point?
questions.fun_fact: He became the third Finnish world champion, after Keke Rosberg and Mika Häkkinen.

questions.text: What color jersey is worn by the overall leader of the Tour de France?
questions.fun_fact: The leader's jersey was introduced during the 1919 Tour, 16 years after the first race.

questions.text: In which year was the first Tour de France held?
questions.fun_fact: Maurice Garin won the first Tour, which had just six stages.

questions.text: What color jersey is worn by the overall leader of the Giro d'Italia?
questions.fun_fact: The color matches the pink pages of La Gazzetta dello Sport, the newspaper that founded the race.

questions.text: Which Belgian cyclist, nicknamed 'The Cannibal', won the Tour de France five times?
questions.fun_fact: In 1969 he won the overall, points and mountains classifications at the same Tour.

questions.text: Which Spanish rider won five consecutive Tours de France from 1991 to 1995?
questions.fun_fact: He also won the Olympic road time trial at the 1996 Atlanta Games.

questions.text: Which golf major is played every year at Augusta National Golf Club?
questions.fun_fact: Augusta National was co-founded by Bobby Jones, one of the greatest amateur golfers.

questions.text: In golf, what is a score of one stroke under par on a hole called?
questions.fun_fact: Three under par on a single hole is called an albatross, or double eagle.

questions.text: Which biennial men's golf event pits a team of European professionals against the United States?
questions.fun_fact: It is named after Samuel Ryder, an English businessman who donated the trophy.

questions.text: Which Scottish golf course is widely known as the 'Home of Golf'?
questions.fun_fact: It only became known as the Old Course after the New Course opened beside it in 1895.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of clubs a golfer may carry in a round under the Rules of Golf?
questions.fun_fact: Fourteen is only a maximum; players who carry their own bags sometimes take just the odd-numbered irons.

questions.text: Which Scottish club hosted the first Open Championship in 1860?
questions.fun_fact: Willie Park Sr. won it over three rounds of Prestwick's 12-hole course.

questions.text: Which country hosted the first Ryder Cup held in continental Europe, in 1997?
questions.fun_fact: Seve Ballesteros captained Europe to victory at Valderrama.

questions.text: What is the standard diameter of the hole on a golf green?
questions.fun_fact: The hole must also be at least 10 cm (4 in) deep.

questions.text: What is the official distance of a marathon?
questions.fun_fact: The distance was fixed in 1921, based on the course used at the 1908 London Olympics.

questions.text: How many events make up the men's decathlon?
questions.fun_fact: The events are spread over two consecutive days, finishing with the 1,500 m.

questions.text: How long is one lap of the inside lane on a standard outdoor athletics track?
questions.fun_fact: Indoor tracks are usually half as long, at 200 m per lap.

questions.text: Who in 1954 became the first person to run a mile in under four minutes?
questions.fun_fact: He ran 3:59.4 on the Iffley Road track in Oxford.

questions.text: Which Ethiopian runner won the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome running barefoot?
questions.fun_fact: He won again at Tokyo 1964, becoming the first athlete to retain the Olympic marathon title.

questions.text: The 'Fosbury Flop' is a technique used in which athletics event?
questions.fun_fact: Dick Fosbury won Olympic gold with it at the 1968 Mexico City Games.

questions.text: How many hurdles does a runner clear in the men's 110 m hurdles?
questions.fun_fact: In the men's race each hurdle stands 1.067 m (42 in) high.

questions.text: What is the standard distance of the Olympic steeplechase in athletics?
questions.fun_fact: Runners clear 28 barriers and seven water jumps over the full distance.

questions.text: How much does the shot weigh in senior men's shot put?
questions.fun_fact: That is 16 pounds; senior women throw a 4 kg shot.

questions.text: In which city did Eliud Kipchoge run a marathon distance in under two hours in 2019?
questions.fun_fact: His time of 1:59:40 was not a record, since rotating pacers and other aids were used.

questions.text: How long is an Olympic-size swimming pool?
questions.fun_fact: Short-course events use 25 m pools, so a 100 m race there takes four lengths.

questions.text: How many players per team are in the water at one time in water polo?
questions.fun_fact: Water polo has been on the Olympic program since 1900, making it one of the oldest Olympic team sports.

questions.text: How many points is the black ball worth in snooker?
questions.fun_fact: A maximum break of 147 means potting all 15 reds, each with a black, then all the colors.

questions.text: Since 2001, a game of table tennis has been played to how many points?
questions.fun_fact: A year earlier, the ball was enlarged from 38 mm to 40 mm in diameter.

questions.text: How many feathers does a traditional badminton shuttlecock have?
questions.fun_fact: The feathers for top-level shuttlecocks traditionally come from geese or ducks.

questions.text: How many players are on each team in standard outdoor polo?
questions.fun_fact: A polo match is divided into timed periods called chukkas.

questions.text: What is the name of the ring in which sumo wrestlers compete?
questions.fun_fact: A dohyō is 4.55 m (15 ft) across and bounded by partly buried rice-straw bales.

questions.text: Which stroke is swum first in a swimming medley relay?
questions.fun_fact: The individual medley uses a different order: butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, then freestyle.

questions.text: Taekwondo is a martial art that originated in which country?
questions.fun_fact: Taekwondo became a full Olympic medal sport at the Sydney 2000 Games.

questions.text: Which martial art is known as 'the art of eight limbs'?
questions.fun_fact: Thailand celebrates Muay Thai Day every year on March 17.

questions.text: Which martial art did Kanō Jigorō found in 1882?
questions.fun_fact: Judo made its Olympic debut at the 1964 Games in Tokyo.

questions.text: Capoeira, a martial art that blends dance, acrobatics and music, developed in which country?
questions.fun_fact: The capoeira circle was added to UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage list in 2014.

questions.text: What is the bamboo sword used in kendo called?
questions.fun_fact: The word kendo means 'the way of the sword'.

questions.text: Which winter sport combines cross-country skiing with rifle shooting?
questions.fun_fact: Its forerunner, military patrol, was contested at the first Winter Olympics in 1924.

questions.text: In which sport would you see an Axel, a Salchow and a Lutz?
questions.fun_fact: The Axel is named after Norwegian skater Axel Paulsen, who first performed it in 1882.

questions.text: In which Winter Olympic sport do athletes slide head-first and face-down on a small sled?
questions.fun_fact: Skeleton was held at the 1928 and 1948 Games in St. Moritz, then returned for good in 2002.

questions.text: In curling, what is the circular target area called?
questions.fun_fact: The very center of the house is called the button.

questions.text: Granite from which Scottish island is famous for making curling stones?
questions.fun_fact: The other main source of curling stone granite is the Trefor quarry in Wales.

questions.text: In which sport is the Stanley Cup awarded?
questions.fun_fact: The trophy was donated in 1892 by Lord Stanley of Preston, then Canada's Governor General.

questions.text: Hurling is an ancient field sport traditionally played in which country?
questions.fun_fact: The small ball used in hurling is called a sliotar.

questions.text: The Thomas Cup is the men's world team championship in which sport?
questions.fun_fact: Malaya won the first edition, played in 1948–49.

questions.text: In which country was the 1974 'Rumble in the Jungle' boxing match held?
questions.fun_fact: Muhammad Ali beat George Foreman there using his 'rope-a-dope' tactic.

questions.text: The sport of squash was developed around 1830 at which English school?
questions.fun_fact: It grew out of rackets, a game played in London's prisons in the 19th century.

questions.text: Which country won the 1983 America's Cup, ending the United States' 132-year winning run?
questions.fun_fact: The winning yacht, Australia II, used a secret winged keel.

questions.text: Which city hosted the first Asian Games in 1951?
questions.fun_fact: Japan topped the medal table at those first Games.

questions.text: What is the capital of Croatia?
questions.fun_fact: Zagreb grew from two medieval settlements, Kaptol and Gradec, which were merged in the 19th century.

questions.text: The Mediterranean island of Corsica belongs to which country?
questions.fun_fact: Napoleon was born in Ajaccio, Corsica, in 1769, the same year France annexed the island from Genoa.

questions.text: Which country's flag shows a nutmeg?
questions.fun_fact: The nutmeg stands for the islands' main export and was kept from the previous flag.

questions.text: What is the capital of Cyprus?
questions.fun_fact: Nicosia's old city is ringed by star-shaped Venetian walls, built in 1567, with 11 bastions.

questions.text: The Atlantic island of Madeira belongs to which country?
questions.fun_fact: Its name is Portuguese for 'wood', for the dense forests that covered it when Portuguese sailors claimed it in 1419.

questions.text: Ngerulmud is the capital of which country?
questions.fun_fact: Ngerulmud replaced Koror as Palau's capital in 2006.

questions.text: The Gallic rooster is a national symbol of which country?
questions.fun_fact: The rooster stands for the French people, while Marianne represents the French Republic.

questions.text: The bald eagle is the national bird of which country?
questions.fun_fact: The bald eagle has appeared on the Great Seal of the United States since 1782.

questions.text: The golden wattle is the national floral emblem of which country?
questions.fun_fact: The golden wattle became Australia's official floral emblem in 1988.

questions.text: The Taj Mahal stands in which Indian city?
questions.fun_fact: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in 1631.

questions.text: Kruger National Park, one of Africa's largest game reserves, is in which country?
questions.fun_fact: The park stretches about 360 km from north to south.

questions.text: The island of Bali belongs to which country?
questions.fun_fact: Bali's subak irrigation system for rice fields, in use since the 9th century, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.text: Which city is the official capital of Côte d'Ivoire?
questions.fun_fact: Yamoussoukro became the legal capital in 1983, though Abidjan keeps several political functions.

questions.text: Tallinn is the capital of which country?
questions.fun_fact: Tallinn's Old Town is one of the best-preserved medieval cities in Europe.

questions.text: Edinburgh is the capital of which part of the United Kingdom?
questions.fun_fact: Edinburgh has been recognized as Scotland's capital since at least the 15th century.

questions.text: The king protea is the national flower of which country?
questions.fun_fact: Its flower head can be up to about 30 cm across, the largest of any protea.

questions.text: Which country was known as Northern Rhodesia until 1964?
questions.fun_fact: The name Zambia comes from the Zambezi River, which forms much of its southern border.

questions.text: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.fun_fact: Vatican City became a sovereign state in 1929 under the Lateran Treaty.

questions.text: Which country's flag features a Sisserou parrot?
questions.fun_fact: It is one of the few national flags that contain the color purple.

questions.text: Which city was Kazakhstan's capital until 1997?
questions.fun_fact: Almaty was known as Alma-Ata during the Soviet era.

questions.text: Which of these South American countries is landlocked?
questions.fun_fact: Paraguay and Bolivia are the only landlocked countries in South America.

questions.text: Bavaria, home of Munich and Oktoberfest, is a state of which country?
questions.fun_fact: Bavaria is the largest of Germany's 16 states by area.

questions.text: Which city is the official capital of Bolivia under its constitution?
questions.fun_fact: At about 2,790 m, Sucre is one of the highest capital cities in the world.

questions.text: The name of Montenegro means what?
questions.fun_fact: In the local language the country is called Crna Gora, which also means 'Black Mountain'.

questions.text: What is the capital of Mexico?
questions.fun_fact: Mexico City sits about 2,240 m above sea level, in a highland valley that once held large lakes.

questions.text: Which West African country was called Dahomey until 1975?
questions.fun_fact: The new name came from the Bight of Benin, which is itself named after the old Kingdom of Benin in modern Nigeria.

questions.text: The name Argentina comes from the Latin word for which metal?
questions.fun_fact: Argentina is the second-largest country in South America by area.

questions.text: The Algarve, a coastal region famous for its beaches, is in which country?
questions.fun_fact: The Algarve is the southernmost region of mainland Portugal.

questions.text: Funafuti is the capital of which country?
questions.fun_fact: Tuvalu has long earned government revenue by leasing out its '.tv' internet domain.

questions.text: What is the capital of the Bahamas?
questions.fun_fact: Nassau is named after William of Orange-Nassau, who became King of England in 1689.

questions.text: Which African country was long known to Europeans as Abyssinia?
questions.fun_fact: Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa, is home to the headquarters of the African Union.

questions.text: Which part of the United Kingdom has a red dragon on its flag?
questions.fun_fact: The red dragon flag was officially recognized as the Welsh national flag only in 1959.

questions.text: Moroni is the capital of which country?
questions.fun_fact: The Comoros lie at the northern end of the Mozambique Channel, between Africa and Madagascar.

questions.text: The island of New Guinea is shared by Papua New Guinea and which country?
questions.fun_fact: New Guinea is the world's second-largest island, after Greenland.

questions.text: Quebec is a province of which country?
questions.fun_fact: Quebec is Canada's largest province by area.

questions.text: Which country's flag has a vertical stripe of five traditional carpet designs?
questions.fun_fact: The five carpet patterns, called güls, represent the country's five major tribes.

questions.text: What is the capital of Lithuania?
questions.fun_fact: Vilnius's Old Town is considered one of the largest and best-preserved old towns in Europe.

questions.text: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.fun_fact: The name Tokyo means 'Eastern Capital' in Japanese.

questions.text: Which country is called 'Sakartvelo' by its own people?
questions.fun_fact: 'Sakartvelo' comes from Kartli, the historic central region of the country.

questions.text: Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with which country?
questions.fun_fact: Hispaniola is the most populous island in the West Indies.

questions.text: The Flemish Region, home to Antwerp and Ghent, is part of which country?
questions.fun_fact: Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.

questions.text: Which South American country is named after the equator?
questions.fun_fact: Ecuador became a separate sovereign state in 1830, after leaving Gran Colombia.

questions.text: Nukuʻalofa is the capital of which country?
questions.fun_fact: Nukuʻalofa lies on the north coast of Tongatapu, Tonga's main island.

questions.text: Garuda, a mythical eagle-like bird, forms the national emblem of which country?
questions.fun_fact: The Garuda grips a scroll with the national motto, 'Bhinneka Tunggal Ika', meaning 'Unity in Diversity'.

questions.text: Which is the largest country in the Caribbean by area?
questions.fun_fact: Besides its main island, Cuba includes more than 4,000 smaller islands, islets and cays.

questions.text: Which is the largest landlocked country in the world?
questions.fun_fact: Kazakhstan is also the ninth-largest country in the world by area.

questions.text: Which country's name is usually explained as meaning 'little Venice'?
questions.fun_fact: Explorers were reminded of Venice by stilt houses built over the water of Lake Maracaibo.

questions.text: Which country is a city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula?
questions.fun_fact: Besides its main island, Singapore includes more than 60 smaller islands and islets.

questions.text: Liberia's capital, Monrovia, was named in 1824 in honor of which American statesman?
questions.fun_fact: Before 1824 the settlement was called Christopolis.

questions.text: The name of Sierra Leone refers to mountains named after which animal?
questions.fun_fact: Pedro de Sintra named them Serra Leoa, Portuguese for 'lioness mountains', in 1462.

questions.text: The Philippines is named after which Spanish king?
questions.fun_fact: Explorer Ruy López de Villalobos coined the name in 1543, when Philip was still a prince.

questions.text: The islands of Santorini and Mykonos belong to which country?
questions.fun_fact: Santorini is the largest island of a small ring of islands around a sea-filled volcanic caldera.

questions.text: What is the capital of Vanuatu?
questions.fun_fact: Before independence, Vanuatu was the New Hebrides, ruled jointly by Britain and France.

questions.text: Which country was called the Gold Coast before its independence in 1957?
questions.fun_fact: The new name honored the medieval Ghana Empire, which lay far to the northwest.

questions.text: The city of Dubai is in which country?
questions.fun_fact: Dubai is one of the seven emirates that make up the UAE.

questions.text: Which country's flag has a different emblem on its front and its back?
questions.fun_fact: The front shows the national seal, while the back shows the seal of the Treasury.

questions.text: Sofia is the capital of which country?
questions.fun_fact: In Roman times the city was known as Serdica.

questions.text: What is the capital of the United Kingdom?
questions.fun_fact: The Romans founded London as Londinium almost 2,000 years ago.

questions.text: Which Croatian city was the center of the old Republic of Ragusa?
questions.fun_fact: The Republic of Ragusa was an independent maritime state until 1808.

questions.text: Which musical instrument is the national emblem of Ireland?
questions.fun_fact: The harp was adopted as the emblem of the Irish Free State in 1922.

questions.text: The Okavango Delta, a huge inland wetland, is in which country?
questions.fun_fact: It is one of the few large inland deltas whose waters never flow into a sea or ocean.

questions.text: What is the capital of Egypt?
questions.fun_fact: Cairo was founded in 969 and became the capital of the Fatimid Caliphate in 973.

questions.text: Cameroon's name comes from the Portuguese word for which animals?
questions.fun_fact: Portuguese sailors called the Wouri River the 'Rio dos Camarões', the 'River of Shrimps'.

questions.text: What is the capital of Bangladesh?
questions.fun_fact: One of Dhaka's nicknames is the 'City of Rickshaws'.

questions.text: Which is the largest country in South America by area?
