questions.fun_fact: Para comes from earlier pora, a combination of por and a.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ella siempre se ___ a las siete."?
questions.fun_fact: Levantar may come from Latin levāns, the present participle of levō, "to raise".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "buscar" mean?
questions.fun_fact: The origin of buscar is unknown; it may be related to bosque, "forest".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "leer" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Leer comes from Latin legō, "to collect, to read"; English "legend" is a cognate.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "luggage"?
questions.fun_fact: Equipaje was borrowed from French équipage.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ayer nosotros ___ una película."?
questions.fun_fact: Ver comes from Latin vidēre; its borrowed doublet is video.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ayer ella se ___ de Pedro."?
questions.fun_fact: Enamorar is en- plus amor plus -ar; the reflexive enamorarse takes de.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "En la nevera ___ leche y huevos."?
questions.fun_fact: Hay comes from Old Spanish ha ý, "it has there"; compare French il y a.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "No lo ___ ahí, por favor."?
questions.fun_fact: Poner comes from Latin pōnō; English "position" and "post" are related.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "embarrassment"?
questions.fun_fact: Vergüenza comes from Latin verēcundia, from verēcundus, "feeling shame".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "regalo" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Regalo likely comes from French régal, "treat"; English "gala" has the same ancestor.

questions.text: What does the Spanish expression "lo siento" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Lo siento is literally "I feel it", from the verb sentir.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "stubborn"?
questions.fun_fact: Terco is first attested in the fifteenth century; its origin is debated.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "La nieve es ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Blanco comes from Latin blancus, from a Germanic word meaning "white, bright".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "street"?
questions.fun_fact: Calle comes from Latin callis, a word for a path or track.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Mi hermana es más alta ___ yo."?
questions.fun_fact: Que comes from Latin quid but took over the jobs of Latin quod and quia.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Me gusta ___ en el mar."?
questions.fun_fact: Nadar also means "to be swimming in" something, used with en.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "domingo" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Domingo is a shortening of Late Latin diēs Dominicus, "day of the Lord".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "A mí me ___ los gatos."?
questions.fun_fact: Gustar was borrowed from Latin gustāre, "to taste", replacing Old Spanish gostar.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "neighborhood"?
questions.fun_fact: Barrio comes from Arabic barriyy, "exterior", first naming a city's outer parts.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "water"?
questions.fun_fact: Agua comes from Latin aqua; French eau and Italian acqua are cognates.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "cocinar" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Cocinar comes from Late Latin cocīnāre, from Latin coquīnāre.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "wallet"?
questions.fun_fact: Billetera is billete, "banknote", plus -era; in Spain cartera is the more usual word.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to speak"?
questions.fun_fact: Hablar comes from Latin fābulārī via Old Spanish fablar; its doublet is fabular.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "cabeza" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Cabeza comes from Vulgar Latin capitia, related to Latin caput, "head".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "bridge"?
questions.fun_fact: Puente comes from Latin pōns; French pont and Italian ponte are cognates.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "playa" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Playa comes from Late Latin plagia; French plage and Italian spiaggia are cognates.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "stingy"?
questions.fun_fact: Tacaño probably comes from Hebrew takaná, "ordinance".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "harvest"?
questions.fun_fact: Cosecha comes from older cogecha, ultimately from Latin colligō, "to gather".

questions.text: What does the Spanish expression "meter la pata" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Literally "to put in the paw"; English says "to put one's foot in one's mouth".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "ladder"?
questions.fun_fact: Escalera comes from Late Latin scālāria, from scālae, "steps"; English "escalator" is related.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to complain"?
questions.fun_fact: Quejarse goes back to Latin quassāre; English "quash" is a cognate.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to catch up with"?
questions.fun_fact: Alcanzar goes back to Vulgar Latin *incalciāre, related to calx, "heel".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Antes de que ___ la película, vamos a comprar palomitas."?
questions.fun_fact: Empezar is en- plus pieza, "piece", plus -ar: literally "to break off a piece".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Hoy ___ mucho calor."?
questions.fun_fact: Calor comes from Latin calor, from caleō, "to be hot"; English "calorie" is related.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to boast"?
questions.fun_fact: Presumir comes from Latin praesūmere; it means both "to presume" and "to boast".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Quiero que tú ___ conmigo."?
questions.fun_fact: Venir comes from Latin venīre; its present subjunctive is irregular: vengas, venga.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "queso" mean?
questions.fun_fact: In Spain, queso is also a colloquial word for "foot".

questions.text: What does the Spanish expression "costar un ojo de la cara" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Literally "to cost an eye of the face"; a synonym is costar un Perú.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ellos ___ en sus vacaciones todo el día."?
questions.fun_fact: Pensar comes from Latin pēnsāre; its doublet pesar means "to weigh".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "gato" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Gato comes from Late Latin cattus; French chat and Italian gatto are cognates.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "desahogarse" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Desahogar is des- plus ahogar; it also means "to unburden" and "to relieve".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "tired"?
questions.fun_fact: Cansado is the past participle of cansar, "to tire".

questions.text: Spanish: which form fills the gap in "Cuando llegué, ellos ya ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Salir comes from Latin saliō, "to leap"; English "sally" is a cognate.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "No hay nadie que ___ la respuesta."?
questions.fun_fact: Saber comes from Latin sapiō, "to taste, to know"; English "savvy" is a cognate.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Me alegro de que ___ venido."?
questions.fun_fact: Alegrar comes from alegre, "cheerful"; alegrarse de que takes the subjunctive.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Se me ___ el vaso."?
questions.fun_fact: Caer comes from Latin cadeō; French choir is a cognate.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "vecino" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Vecino comes from Latin vīcīnus; English "vicinity" is a cognate.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "soap"?
questions.fun_fact: Jabón comes from Old Spanish xabon, which goes back to a Germanic word.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "calcetines" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Calcetín is built from calceta, "tights", plus -ín.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "cold (not hot)"?
questions.fun_fact: Frío comes from Latin frīgidus, "cold".

questions.text: What does the Spanish expression "echar una mano" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Literally "to throw a hand"; a synonym is echar un cable, "to throw a cable".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "cumpleaños" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Cumpleaños is literally "year-fulfiller", from cumplir, "to fulfill", and año.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to arrive"?
questions.fun_fact: Llegar comes from Latin applicō, "to land, to reach the coast", a sailor's word.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "pan" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Pan comes from Latin pānis; French pain and Italian pane are cognates.

questions.text: What does the Spanish expression "no tener pelos en la lengua" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Literally "to have no hairs on the tongue".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ayer yo ___ tres kilómetros."?
questions.fun_fact: Correr comes from Latin currō, "to run"; it also means "to flow".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "rojo" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Rojo comes from Old Spanish roxo, from Latin russeus, a variant of russus.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Esta camisa es ___ cara."?
questions.fun_fact: Demasiado is built from demasía, "excess", plus -ado; before an adjective it stays invariable.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Los niños ___ en el parque."?
questions.fun_fact: Jugar comes from Latin iocor; its u-ue stem change is unique among Spanish verbs.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "umbrella"?
questions.fun_fact: Paraguas is literally "stops waters", from parar, "to stop", and agua.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to wait"?
questions.fun_fact: Esperar covers "to hope", "to expect" and "to wait".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "¿Dónde ___ tú?"?
questions.fun_fact: Vivir comes from Latin vīvere; Old Spanish also had the forms bivir and viver.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "libro" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Libro was borrowed from Latin liber; French livre and Portuguese livro are cognates.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Me duele ___ estómago."?
questions.fun_fact: Estómago comes from Greek stómakhos, "gullet, stomach", from stóma, "mouth".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Es la persona con ___ trabajo."?
questions.fun_fact: Quien comes from Latin quem, the accusative of quī.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "ciudad" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Ciudad was cibdat in Old Spanish; English "city" is a cognate.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to wake up"?
questions.fun_fact: Despertar may come from despierto, "awake", plus -ar.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ella ___ una carta."?
questions.fun_fact: Escribir comes from Latin scrībere via Old Spanish escrivir.

questions.text: What does the Spanish expression "tomar el pelo" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Literally "to take the hair"; it may come from an old prank of pulling off a wig.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Mi padre ___ en una oficina."?
questions.fun_fact: Trabajar comes from Vulgar Latin *tripāliāre, "to torment", and once also meant "to suffer".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "semana" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Semana comes from Late Latin septimāna, related to septimus, "seventh".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to lose"?
questions.fun_fact: Perder comes from Latin perdō; English "perdition" is a cognate.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "chair"?
questions.fun_fact: Silla is cognate with French selle and Italian sella, which mean "saddle".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "librería" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Librería is libro plus -ería; in some places it also means "bookcase".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je ___ ai vus hier."?
questions.fun_fact: Voir takes a direct object, so the pronoun is les, and the participle vus agrees with it.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je voudrais ___ café, s'il vous plaît."?
questions.fun_fact: Café reached French via Italian caffè and Ottoman Turkish kahve, from Arabic qahwa.

questions.text: Which French word means "ladybug"?
questions.fun_fact: Coccinelle comes from the Latin name Coccinella, from coccinus, "scarlet".

questions.text: Which French word means "to forget"?
questions.fun_fact: Oublier goes back to Latin oblivisci, "to forget", via its past participle oblitus.

questions.text: Which French phrase means "to be late"?
questions.fun_fact: Retard is formed from the verb retarder, "to delay".

questions.text: Which French word means "to fill"?
questions.fun_fact: Remplir is re- plus emplir, "to fill", and its opposite is vider.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il faut que j'___ du courage."?
questions.fun_fact: Avoir has an irregular subjunctive: que j'aie, que tu aies, qu'il ait, qu'ils aient.

questions.text: Which French word means "drawer"?
questions.fun_fact: Tiroir comes from tirer, "to pull": it is something you pull out.

questions.text: Which French word means "stairs"?
questions.fun_fact: Escalier came into French via Occitan escalier, from Late Latin scalarium, from scala, "ladder".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Nous ___ au cinéma ce soir."?
questions.fun_fact: The forms of aller come from several Latin verbs, so "je vais" and "nous allons" look very different.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "___ heure est-il ?"?
questions.fun_fact: Heure is feminine, so it takes quelle; "Quelle heure est-il ?" is literally "what hour is it?".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je ___ français."?
questions.fun_fact: Parler goes back to Latin parabolare, from parabola, "parable, comparison".

questions.text: What does "flâner" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: English borrowed "flâneur", a leisurely wanderer, from the French noun built on this verb.

questions.text: Which French word means "umbrella"?
questions.fun_fact: Parapluie is para-, "guarding against", plus pluie, "rain".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Mon frère ___ très grand."?
questions.fun_fact: Before a noun grand can mean "great" (un grand homme), but after it only "tall" (un homme grand).

questions.text: What does "attendre" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Attendre is a false friend of English "attend": it means "to wait for" or "to expect".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Elle ___ de la musique tous les soirs."?
questions.fun_fact: Écouter comes from Latin ascultare, a variant of auscultare, which French later borrowed again as ausculter.

questions.text: What does "écureuil" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Écureuil goes back to Latin sciurus, which was itself borrowed from Greek.

questions.text: Which French word means "sidewalk"?
questions.fun_fact: Trottoir is related to trotter, "to trot", and means a path made for walking.

questions.text: Which French word means "mushroom"?
questions.fun_fact: Champignon comes from Vulgar Latin campaniolus, "grows in the field".

questions.text: In France, what meal is "le déjeuner"?
questions.fun_fact: Déjeuner is dé- plus jeûner, "to fast"; in Belgium, Switzerland and Canada it means breakfast, and lunch is le dîner.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Elle ___ une pomme."?
questions.fun_fact: Manger comes from Latin manducare, "to chew".

questions.text: What does "sympa" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Sympa is a clipped form of sympathique, which means "nice" rather than "sympathetic".

questions.text: What does "jeudi" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Jeudi comes from Latin Iovis dies, "day of Jupiter".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Ce sont ___ amis."?
questions.fun_fact: Possessives agree with the thing owned, not the owner: mon livre, ma maison, mes amis.

questions.text: What does "manquer" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: "Tu me manques" works backwards: it is literally "you are missing to me", meaning "I miss you".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je me ___ à sept heures."?
questions.fun_fact: The noun le lever also means "rising": "le lever du soleil" is the sunrise.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Parle-___ !"?
questions.fun_fact: After an affirmative command, me becomes moi ("Parle-moi !"), but "Ne me parle pas !" keeps me.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je suis ___ Paris depuis trois ans."?
questions.fun_fact: The accent on à separates it from a, "has": "il a faim", but "il va à Paris".

questions.text: Which French word means "dandelion"?
questions.fun_fact: Pissenlit is literally "pee in bed", after the plant's diuretic properties; in Switzerland it is also called dent-de-lion.

questions.text: What does "poser un lapin" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: The idiom is literally "to put down a rabbit".

questions.text: Which French word means "friend"?
questions.fun_fact: Ami comes from Latin amicus, like Spanish and Portuguese amigo and Italian amico.

questions.text: In modern French, what kind of shop or place is a "librairie"?
questions.fun_fact: Librairie once meant "library"; the "bookshop" sense, from the 16th century, displaced it.

questions.text: What does "retrouvailles" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Retrouvailles is retrouver, "to find again", plus the suffix -aille, and is chiefly used in the plural.

questions.text: Which French word means "hedgehog"?
questions.fun_fact: Hérisson comes from Latin ericius, "hedgehog".

questions.text: Which French word means "snail"?
questions.fun_fact: Escargot comes from Occitan escargol; in French it is also a teasing word for a slowpoke.

questions.text: Which French word means "apple"?
questions.fun_fact: Pomme comes from Latin poma, the plural of pomum, "fruit".

questions.text: Which French word means "to be bored"?
questions.fun_fact: Ennuyer comes from Late Latin inodiare; besides "to bore", it can also mean "to annoy" or "to worry".

questions.text: What does "débrouiller" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Débrouiller is dé- plus brouiller, "to mix up"; the reflexive se débrouiller means "to get by, to manage".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il boit trop ___ café."?
questions.fun_fact: After expressions of quantity such as trop and beaucoup, French uses bare de: "trop de café".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Les lettres que j'ai ___ sont arrivées."?
questions.fun_fact: Écrire comes from Latin scribere; the participle agrees with a preceding object: "les lettres que j'ai écrites".

questions.text: Which French word means "garlic"?
questions.fun_fact: Ail has two plurals: ails and aulx.

questions.text: What does "merci" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Merci comes from Latin merces, "wages, price"; as a noun it can also mean "mercy".

questions.text: What does "emménager" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Emménager is the opposite of déménager, "to move out" or "to move house".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je regrette qu'il ne ___ pas venir."?
questions.fun_fact: The subjunctive of pouvoir is irregular: que je puisse, que tu puisses, qu'il puisse.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Nous avons ___ le train de huit heures."?
questions.fun_fact: Prendre also covers meals and transport: "prendre un café", "prendre le train".

questions.text: What does "tutoyer" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Tutoyer is built on tu; its counterpart vouvoyer is built on vous.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il y a ___ chien dans le jardin."?
questions.fun_fact: Un comes from Latin unus and doubles as the number "one".

questions.text: What does the French expression "pleuvoir des cordes" mean?
questions.fun_fact: The expression is literally "to rain ropes".

questions.text: Which French word means "daily"?
questions.fun_fact: As a noun, un quotidien is a daily newspaper.

questions.text: What does "grenouille" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Grenouille is a diminutive formation from Latin rana, "frog".

questions.text: What does "néanmoins" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Néanmoins is made of néant, "nothing", plus moins, "less": roughly "nothing less".

questions.text: What does "dépaysement" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Dépaysement is built on pays, "country": the feeling of being out of your usual surroundings.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Ils ___ leurs devoirs."?
questions.fun_fact: Faire is one of very few verbs whose vous form ends in -tes: "vous faites".

questions.text: Which French word means "to improve"?
questions.fun_fact: Améliorer goes back to Latin meliorare, from melior, "better".

questions.text: What does "cadeau" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Cadeau comes from Old Occitan capdel, "ornament", which goes back to Latin capitellum.

questions.text: What does "chien" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Chien comes from Latin canis, "dog"; it also names the hammer of a gun.

questions.text: Which French word means "water"?
questions.fun_fact: Eau comes from Latin aqua, by way of Old French forms such as ewe.

questions.text: Which French word means "to sleep"?
questions.fun_fact: Dormir comes from Latin dormire, and Spanish, Portuguese and Catalan still use the same form, dormir.

questions.text: Which French word means "cherry"?
questions.fun_fact: English borrowed cerise as a color name for a deep pinkish red.

questions.text: What does "pamplemousse" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Pamplemousse was borrowed from Dutch pompelmoes.

questions.text: What does "pneu" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Pneu is short for pneumatique, the old term for a pneumatic tire.

questions.text: What does "fromage" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Fromage comes from Vulgar Latin formaticum, "shaped in a mold".

questions.text: What does "pomme de terre" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Pomme de terre is literally "apple of the earth".

questions.text: Which French word means "to wake up"?
questions.fun_fact: Un réveil is also an alarm clock, from the same verb.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il est parti sans que je le ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Sans comes from Latin sine, like Spanish sin and Italian senza; the conjunction sans que takes the subjunctive.

questions.text: Which French word means "screwdriver"?
questions.fun_fact: Tournevis is tourne, "turns", plus vis, "screw".

questions.text: What does "chaussettes" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Chaussette is chausse, a historical word for stockings or hose, plus the diminutive -ette.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Elle est plus grande ___ moi."?
questions.fun_fact: In comparisons, "plus ... que" means "more than" and "aussi ... que" means "as ... as".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je ne ___ pas la réponse."?
questions.fun_fact: Savoir comes from Latin sapere; in Belgium it is also used in the positive to mean "to be able to".

questions.text: Which French word means "to get used to"?
questions.fun_fact: Habituer is a learned borrowing from Late Latin habituare; without se it means to get someone into a habit.

questions.text: Which French word means "wasp"?
questions.fun_fact: Guêpe comes from a blend of Latin vespa, "wasp", and Frankish *wapsu, both from one Proto-Indo-European word for "wasp".

questions.text: Which French word means "shoelace"?
questions.fun_fact: Lacet also means a hairpin bend: a "route en lacets" is a winding road.

questions.text: Which French word means "tablecloth"?
questions.fun_fact: Nappe comes from Latin mappa; it can also mean a layer or sheet, such as a sheet of water.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Quand j'étais petit, je ___ dans le parc tous les jours."?
questions.fun_fact: Games take à (jouer au foot) but instruments take de (jouer du piano).

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je cherche ___ clé."?
questions.fun_fact: Clé is also spelled clef, the older form that clé had replaced by 1845; it also means a musical clef.

questions.text: Which French word means "school"?
questions.fun_fact: École is an early borrowing from Latin schola, which comes from Greek scholē.

questions.text: Which French word means "to hurry up"?
questions.fun_fact: Dépêcher is formed from dé- plus empêcher, "to hinder": to free from obstacles.

questions.text: What does "papillon" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: A "nœud papillon" is a bow tie, literally a "butterfly knot".

questions.text: Which French word means "bread"?
questions.fun_fact: Pain comes from Latin panis; in informal French it can also mean a punch.

questions.text: Which French word means "to lend"?
questions.fun_fact: Prêter comes from Latin praestare, like Spanish and Portuguese prestar and Italian prestare.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Ils se sont ___ hier."?
questions.fun_fact: Voir comes from Latin videre; the participle of "se voir" agrees here because se is the object.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Si j'avais de l'argent, j'___ une voiture."?
questions.fun_fact: Acheter takes a grave accent when the next syllable has a silent e: j'achète, j'achèterais, but nous achetons.

questions.text: What does "gaufre" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Gaufre comes from Frankish *wāfilu and is a cousin of English "waffle".

questions.text: What does "tout de suite" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: English borrowed "tout de suite" too, sometimes spelled "toot sweet".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Voici le livre ___ je t'ai parlé."?
questions.fun_fact: Dont comes from Latin de unde, "from where", and replaces de plus a relative pronoun.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Tu ___ quel âge ?"?
questions.fun_fact: French uses avoir, "to have", for age: "j'ai vingt ans" is literally "I have twenty years".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Nous ___ ensemble depuis dix ans."?
questions.fun_fact: Vivre comes from Latin vivere; past forms in véc-, as in j'ai vécu, come from the Latin perfect vixi.

questions.text: What does "avoir le cafard" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: The phrase is traced to Baudelaire's Les Fleurs du mal (1857), after which le cafard came to mean deep gloom.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Hier, je ___ allé au marché."?
questions.fun_fact: Verbs of movement such as aller, venir and partir form the passé composé with être, not avoir.

questions.text: Which French word means "pillow"?
questions.fun_fact: Oreiller comes from oreille, "ear": the thing you rest your ear on.

questions.text: What does "ordinateur" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: The philologist Jacques Perret coined ordinateur in 1955, after a request from IBM France.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Elle a ___ ses clés."?
questions.fun_fact: Perdre comes from Latin perdere; the reflexive se perdre means "to get lost".

questions.text: Which French word means "house"?
questions.fun_fact: Maison comes from Latin mansio, "dwelling", from manere, "to stay", which also gave French manoir.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il faut que tu ___ ton travail."?
questions.fun_fact: Finir comes from Latin finire; its Old French form fenir was reshaped under the influence of fin, "end".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je vais ___ France cet été."?
questions.fun_fact: Feminine countries take en (en France), as do masculine ones starting with a vowel; others take au (au Japon).

questions.text: Which French word means "suddenly"?
questions.fun_fact: Soudain comes from Latin subitaneus, "sudden", and works both as an adjective and as an adverb.

questions.text: In everyday French, what does "actuellement" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Actuellement is a false friend: its synonyms are en ce moment and maintenant, and only rarely does it mean "in actuality".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Bien qu'il ___ fatigué, il a continué."?
questions.fun_fact: Bien que, "although", is always followed by the subjunctive: "bien qu'il soit fatigué".

questions.text: What does "bonjour" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Bonjour is bon, "good", plus jour, "day"; in North America it can also be said as goodbye.

questions.text: What does "faire la grasse matinée" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: The expression is literally "to do the fat morning".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Ils ___ des enfants."?
questions.fun_fact: Ont is from Latin habent, "they have"; do not confuse it with on, "one" or "we", or with sont.

questions.text: What does "bavarder" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Bavarder is formed from the adjective bavard, "talkative".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "J'habite ici ___ 2019."?
questions.fun_fact: Depuis goes back to Latin de post; French uses the present tense with it: j'habite ici depuis 2019.

questions.text: Which French word means "ladle"?
questions.fun_fact: Louche also exists as an adjective meaning "shady" or "suspicious".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Quand j'ai appelé, elle ___ déjà sortie."?
questions.fun_fact: Sortir takes être in compound tenses, so the pluperfect is elle était sortie.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "La fille ___ parle est ma cousine."?
questions.fun_fact: Qui is the subject relative pronoun; que is the object: la fille que je vois.

questions.text: In French, what is "la rentrée" in early September?
questions.fun_fact: Rentrée also simply means a return; la rentrée scolaire is the start of the school year.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "___ habites-tu ?"?
questions.fun_fact: Où has a grave accent to tell it apart from ou, "or".

questions.text: Which French word means "to wash"?
questions.fun_fact: Laver comes from Latin lavare; a machine à laver is a washing machine.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Quand j'étais enfant, nous ___ l'été à la mer."?
questions.fun_fact: Passer also means "to spend time": passer l'été, passer une semaine.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Quoi que tu ___, je te crois."?
questions.fun_fact: Quoi que, in two words, means "whatever" and takes the subjunctive; quoique means "although".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je me ___ de ce jour."?
questions.fun_fact: Souvenir is also a noun meaning "memory" or "keepsake", which English borrowed.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Après ___ mangé, ils sont partis."?
questions.fun_fact: Après takes a past infinitive: après avoir mangé, but après être parti for être verbs.

questions.text: Which French word means "eyelash"?
questions.fun_fact: Cil comes from Latin cilium; sourcil, "eyebrow", comes from Latin supercilium.

questions.text: What does "tant mieux" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Its opposite is tant pis, "too bad".

questions.text: What does "fête" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Fête comes from Middle French feste; the circumflex marks the lost s. English borrowed the word as fête.

questions.text: Which French word means "to deserve"?
questions.fun_fact: Mériter comes from mérite, "merit", and replaced an older verb merir.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Elle ___ de Lyon."?
questions.fun_fact: Venir de plus an infinitive means "to have just": elle vient de partir is "she has just left".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Les enfants jouent ___ le jardin."?
questions.fun_fact: Dans comes from Latin de intus, "from inside".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Ce gâteau est ___ que l'autre."?
questions.fun_fact: Meilleur, from Latin melior, is the comparative of bon; mieux is for verbs, as in il chante mieux.

questions.text: Which French word means "tomato"?
questions.fun_fact: Tomate came into French from Spanish, which took it from Nahuatl tomatl.

questions.text: Which French word means "tired"?
questions.fun_fact: Fatigué is the past participle of fatiguer; épuisé is a stronger word for "exhausted".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Les ___ sont dans le champ."?
questions.fun_fact: Most nouns ending in -al form the plural in -aux: cheval, chevaux; journal, journaux.

questions.text: Which French word means "to rent"?
questions.fun_fact: Louer comes from Latin locare; a different verb louer means "to praise".

questions.text: What does "s'il vous plaît" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: It is literally "if it pleases you"; the informal form is s'il te plaît.

questions.text: What does "mélanger" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Mélanger comes from the noun mélange, which English borrowed as "mélange".

questions.text: What does "davantage" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Davantage comes from d'avantage, "of advantage"; it simply means "more".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Nous sommes ___ vacances."?
questions.fun_fact: Vacances is almost always plural in French: bonnes vacances ! means "have a good holiday".

questions.text: What does "gentil" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Gentil comes from Latin gentilis, from gens, "clan"; as a noun it can also mean "gentile".

questions.text: Which French word means "knife"?
questions.fun_fact: Couteau comes from Latin cultellus, "little knife".

questions.text: What does "gare" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Gare comes from garer, "to dock"; the verb se garer also means "to park".

questions.text: Which French word means "lawn"?
questions.fun_fact: Pelouse goes back to Latin pilosus, "hairy", through a regional word.

questions.text: Which French word means "stubborn"?
questions.fun_fact: Têtu is built on tête, "head": a stubborn person has a hard head.

questions.text: What does "chuchoter" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Chuchoter is imitative, echoing the hushed sound it describes.

questions.text: What does "se tromper" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Tromper alone means "to deceive", so se tromper is literally "to deceive oneself".

questions.text: Which French word means "lighthouse"?
questions.fun_fact: Phare comes via Latin pharus from Greek Pharos; it also means a car's headlight.

questions.text: Which French word means "to knit"?
questions.fun_fact: Tricoter is related to trique, "stick, cudgel".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il faut que nous ___ à l'heure."?
questions.fun_fact: Arriver comes from Medieval Latin adripare; it can be seen as a- + rive, "riverbank", + -er.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il faut que tu ___ ton manteau."?
questions.fun_fact: Il faut que is followed by the subjunctive, so tu mets becomes que tu mettes.

questions.text: Which French word means "to sweep"?
questions.fun_fact: Balayer is formed from balai, "broom".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Tu vas à Lyon ? Oui, j'___ vais demain."?
questions.fun_fact: Y replaces a place or an à-phrase: j'y vais is "I'm going there".

questions.text: Which French word means "kitchen"?
questions.fun_fact: Cuisine comes from Latin coquina and is a cousin of English kitchen.

questions.text: What does "il s'agit de" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: S'agir is impersonal: it exists only as il s'agit, so je m'agis does not exist in this sense.

questions.text: French: which words fill the gap in "Je ne comprends pas ___ tu dis."?
questions.fun_fact: Ce que is the object form of "what": ce que tu dis; the subject form is ce qui: ce qui se passe.

questions.text: Which French word means "red"?
questions.fun_fact: Rouge comes from Latin rubeus; un carton rouge is a red card in soccer.

questions.text: What does "valoir la peine" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Valoir la peine and valoir le coup both say "to be worth it".

questions.text: Which French word means "suitcase"?
questions.fun_fact: Faire sa valise means "to pack one's suitcase".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Elle est ___ hier soir."?
questions.fun_fact: Partir comes from Latin partire, "to divide", and takes être in the past: elle est partie.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "La table sur ___ j'ai posé le verre est ancienne."?
questions.fun_fact: Lequel is le + quel and agrees with its noun; with à and de it fuses: auquel, duquel.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Si j'avais su, je ne ___ pas venu."?
questions.fun_fact: After si plus the pluperfect, the main clause takes the past conditional: je ne serais pas venu.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il me parle comme s'il me ___ depuis toujours."?
questions.fun_fact: After comme si, French uses the imperfect or pluperfect: comme s'il me connaissait.

questions.text: What does "emprunter" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Emprunter also means "to take" a road: emprunter l'autoroute is to take the highway.

questions.text: Which French word means "tooth"?
questions.fun_fact: Dent goes back to Latin dens, dentis; une dent de sagesse is a wisdom tooth.

questions.text: What does "dehors" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Dehors comes from Latin de foris, "from outside"; its opposite is dedans.

questions.text: What does "boulangerie" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: A boulangerie sells bread; cakes and pastries come from a pâtisserie, though many shops are both.

questions.text: What does "se méfier de" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Méfie-toi ! is a common warning meaning "watch out".

questions.text: What does "enfin" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Enfin is en + fin, "in the end"; it is also a filler like "well" or "I mean".

questions.text: Which French word means "ceiling"?
questions.fun_fact: Plafond is plat, "flat", plus fond, "bottom"; it also means an upper limit, like a price cap.

questions.text: Which French word means "book"?
questions.fun_fact: Livre is masculine for "book" but feminine for "pound": un livre, but une livre sterling.

questions.text: What does "gaspiller" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: The origin of gaspiller is uncertain; le gaspillage alimentaire is "food waste".

questions.text: What does "bientôt" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Bientôt is bien, "very", plus tôt, "early"; à bientôt means "see you soon".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Nous ___ de l'eau."?
questions.fun_fact: Boire comes from Latin bibere and has a changing stem: nous buvons, but ils boivent.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Les enfants aiment ___ école."?
questions.fun_fact: As a possessive, leur takes an s only before plural nouns: leur école, leurs amis.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il fait très ___ en été."?
questions.fun_fact: French weather phrases use faire: il fait chaud is literally "it makes hot".

questions.text: Which French word means "sheep"?
questions.fun_fact: Mouton also means mutton, the meat; un mouton noir is a "black sheep".

questions.text: Which French word means "to guess"?
questions.fun_fact: Deviner comes from Latin divinare; a devin is a soothsayer, and divin means "divine".

questions.text: What does "voiture" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Voiture comes from Latin vectura; le covoiturage is French for carpooling.

questions.text: What does "chat" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Chat comes from Late Latin cattus; a female cat is une chatte.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je parle à Marie : je ___ parle souvent."?
questions.fun_fact: Lui replaces à plus a person, for either gender: je lui parle can mean "I speak to him" or "to her".

questions.text: What does "pourvu que" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Pourvu que takes the subjunctive; as a wish, "Pourvu que ça marche !" means "let's hope it works".

questions.text: What does "lait" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Lait comes from Latin lac, lactis; café au lait is literally "coffee with milk".

questions.text: Which French word means "to ask"?
questions.fun_fact: Demander is a false friend of English demand: it means "to ask", not "to demand".

questions.text: Which French word means "new"?
questions.fun_fact: Nouveau goes back to Latin novellus; English borrowed it in "nouveau riche" and "art nouveau".

questions.text: What does "faire semblant" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Faire semblant de plus an infinitive means "to pretend to": il a fait semblant de dormir.

questions.text: Which French word means "tomorrow"?
questions.fun_fact: Demain comes from Latin de mane, "early in the morning".

questions.text: Which French word means "street"?
questions.fun_fact: Rue comes from Latin ruga, which meant "wrinkle" or "furrow".

questions.text: Which French word means "to shed tears"?
questions.fun_fact: Pleurer comes from Latin plorare, "to cry out"; pleurer comme une madeleine means to cry one's eyes out.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je vais ___ le journal."?
questions.fun_fact: Lire comes from Latin legere; lire entre les lignes means "to read between the lines".

questions.text: What does "tellement" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Tellement is tel, "such", plus -ment: je suis tellement content is "I am so happy".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Én ___ élek."?
questions.fun_fact: Magyarország means "land of the Magyars"; ország is the word for "country".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "szia" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Szia is informal and works as both a greeting and a farewell.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "library"?
questions.fun_fact: Könyvtár is könyv, "book", plus tár, "storehouse".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Én kávét ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Inni, "to drink", is an -ik verb: its 3rd person singular ends in -ik (iszik).

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "köszönöm" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Köszönöm is "I thank"; the longer form is Köszönöm szépen, "thank you very much".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "spring (the season)"?
questions.fun_fact: Do not confuse tavasz with tavaly, which means "last year".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Ő magyarul ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Beszél, "speaks", is related to the noun beszéd, "speech".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "kenyér" mean?
questions.fun_fact: A kenyérpirító, "toaster", literally means "bread roaster".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "summer"?
questions.fun_fact: Nyár gives the verb nyaral, "to spend the summer holiday".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Két ___ van a kertben."?
questions.fun_fact: After a number a Hungarian noun stays singular: két fa, öt fa. Fa means both "tree" and "wood".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "víz" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Vizes, "wet", is víz plus the ending -es, and the long í turns short.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "chair"?
questions.fun_fact: A karosszék is an armchair, literally an "arm chair".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Tegnap én moziban ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Voltam is the past of lenni, "to be": voltam, voltál, volt.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "tej" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Tej also appears in tejföl, sour cream: tej plus föl, an old word for cream.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "door"?
questions.fun_fact: Kapu is the word for a gate; ajtó is for a door.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "A könyv az ___ van."?
questions.fun_fact: The ending -on/-en/-ön means "on" a surface: asztalon, ablakon.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "kutya" mean?
questions.fun_fact: A kutyaház is a doghouse; Hungarian forms compounds just like English.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "window"?
questions.fun_fact: A windshield wiper is an ablaktörlő, literally a "window wiper".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "___ alma piros."?
questions.fun_fact: Hungarian has no grammatical gender. The definite article is a before consonants and az before vowels.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "macska" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Cica is the affectionate or child-speak word for a kitty.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "apple"?
questions.fun_fact: Almás pite is Hungarian apple pie.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Mit ___ te?"?
questions.fun_fact: One verb, csinál, covers both "to do" and "to make".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "iskola" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Iskola comes from Latin schola, the same source as English "school".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "cheese"?
questions.fun_fact: Sajtos pogácsa is a popular Hungarian cheese scone.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Látom a ___."?
questions.fun_fact: The accusative ending is -t, added straight after a vowel: fiú becomes fiút.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "csütörtök" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Csütörtök comes from a Slavic word for "fourth", the fourth day of the week.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "egg"?
questions.fun_fact: Tojás is also the word for Easter eggs: húsvéti tojás.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Ő jól beszél ___."?
questions.fun_fact: The ending -ul/-ül forms language adverbs: magyarul, angolul, németül.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "szerda" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Szerda comes from a Slavic word meaning "middle".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "fish"?
questions.fun_fact: Halászlé is a spicy Hungarian fish soup.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "A ___ megyek moziba."?
questions.fun_fact: The ending -val/-vel assimilates to a consonant: barátom + val gives barátommal, with a double m.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "hétfő" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Hétfő is hét, "week", plus fő, "head": the head of the week.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "mountain"?
questions.fun_fact: Hegy gives hegyvidék, "highland", and the Tokaj wine region is called Hegyalja.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Adok egy könyvet a ___."?
questions.fun_fact: The dative ending follows vowel harmony: -nak after back vowels, -nek after front vowels.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "vonat" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Vonat is built on vonni, "to pull".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "sea"?
questions.fun_fact: Lake Balaton is nicknamed "the Hungarian sea", a magyar tenger.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Ez az én ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Possession is a suffix: könyvem is "my book", könyved is "your book".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "szomszéd" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Szomszéd is a Slavic loanword that entered Hungarian very early.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "forest"?
questions.fun_fact: Erdély, the Hungarian name of Transylvania, is linked to erdő.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Holnap én Pécsre ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Menni is irregular: megyek, mész, megy. Its past stem is ment-, as in mentem.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "esernyő" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Esernyő copies German Regenschirm, "rain screen": es- from esik, "to rain", plus ernyő, "screen".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "flower"?
questions.fun_fact: Virág also means "bloom" and is a common Hungarian given name.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Tegnap én sokat ___."?
questions.fun_fact: The past of enni, "to eat", has the stem et-: ettem, ettél, evett.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "tegnap" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Tegnap and holnap, "yesterday" and "tomorrow", are an easy pair to learn together.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "child"?
questions.fun_fact: Gyermek is the more formal and literary word for "child".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "___ vagy? – Jól, köszönöm."?
questions.fun_fact: Hogy vagy? asks "how are you?"; hogy is also the conjunction "that".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "hűtőszekrény" mean?
questions.fun_fact: It is hűtő, "cooler", plus szekrény, "cabinet".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "grandmother"?
questions.fun_fact: Nagymama is nagy, "big", plus mama; the shorter form is nagyi.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Én éhes ___."?
questions.fun_fact: With a noun in the 3rd person the verb "to be" is dropped: Ő tanár means "he is a teacher".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "fogkefe" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Fog means "tooth" and kefe means "brush".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "shoe"?
questions.fun_fact: A cipőfűző is a shoelace.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "A gyerekek a parkban ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Játszik, "to play", is an -ik verb: játszom, játszol, játszik, but játszanak in the plural.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "szappan" mean?
questions.fun_fact: A soap opera is a szappanopera in Hungarian, a word-for-word copy of the English term.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "hat"?
questions.fun_fact: Kalap also means the cap of a mushroom.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Én a könyvet ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Hungarian verbs have indefinite (olvasok) and definite (olvasom) endings; the definite set is used for a specific object.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "cseresznye" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Meggy is the sour cherry, and meggyleves is a famous chilled Hungarian soup.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "sock"?
questions.fun_fact: Harisnya is the word for stockings or tights.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "A kisbaba már ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Aludni, "to sleep", has the present stem alsz-: alszom, alszol, alszik.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "pillangó" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Lepke is another common Hungarian word for butterfly.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "wallet"?
questions.fun_fact: Pénztárca is pénz, "money", plus tárca, "case".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "A ___ van egy ágy."?
questions.fun_fact: The ending -ban/-ben means "in", and a final -a lengthens to á: szoba becomes szobában.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "bagoly" mean?
questions.fun_fact: The proverb "Bagoly mondja verébnek, hogy nagyfejű" (the owl calls the sparrow big-headed) is the pot calling the kettle black.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "airport"?
questions.fun_fact: Repülőtér is repülő, "flier", plus tér, "space".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Ő ___ jön."?
questions.fun_fact: The ending -ból/-ből means "out of"; olasz means "Italian", so Olaszország is "Italian land".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "kikötő" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Kikötő comes from kikötni, "to moor": ki, "out", plus kötni, "to tie".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "railway station"?
questions.fun_fact: Budapest has the Keleti, "Eastern", pályaudvar.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "___ mész haza?"?
questions.fun_fact: Mikor is "when"; hol is "where", hová "where to" and honnan "where from".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "ügyes" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Ügyes is the common praise "well done" for a child: Ügyes vagy!

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "fork"?
questions.fun_fact: Villa also means a luxury house, as in English.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Van egy ___ kutyám."?
questions.fun_fact: Nagy means "big"; the adverb nagyon, "very", is built on it.

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "bátor" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Bátor once also meant "although"; its shortened form bár is still the everyday word for it.

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "spoon"?
questions.fun_fact: A teáskanál is a teaspoon and an evőkanál, literally "eating spoon", is a tablespoon.

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Ha időm lenne, moziba ___."?
questions.fun_fact: The conditional adds -nék for "I": mennék, "I would go"; aludnék is "I would sleep".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "gyönyörű" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Gyönyörű is stronger than szép, "pretty": it means "gorgeous".

questions.text: Which Hungarian word means "mirror"?
questions.fun_fact: Tükörtojás is a fried egg, literally "mirror egg".

questions.text: Hungarian: which word fills the gap in "Ők tegnap moziban ___."?
questions.fun_fact: Volt is "was"; add -ak and you get voltak, "they were".

questions.text: What does the Hungarian word "öröm" mean?

questions.text: Which of the four fundamental forces is by far the weakest?
