questions.text: The Large Hadron Collider straddles the border between France and which other country?
questions.fun_fact: Its main accelerator ring is about 27 km around and runs in a tunnel underground.

questions.text: In physics, work is calculated as force multiplied by what?
questions.fun_fact: Gaspard-Gustave Coriolis was one of two Frenchmen who introduced the term work in the late 1820s.

questions.text: Which Dutch physicist discovered in 1896 that a magnetic field splits the spectral lines of light?
questions.fun_fact: He shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Hendrik Lorentz, whose electron theory explained the splitting.

questions.text: Which term describes a system's strong response when it is pushed at its own natural rate of vibration?
questions.fun_fact: Pushing a child on a swing at just the right rhythm is an everyday example.

questions.text: Which German mathematician published a theorem in 1918 linking symmetries in physics to conservation laws?
questions.fun_fact: Her theorem links the conservation of energy to the fact that the laws of physics do not change over time.

questions.text: Which principle says that in a flowing fluid, pressure drops where the speed increases?
questions.fun_fact: Swiss scientist Daniel Bernoulli published it in his 1738 book Hydrodynamica.

questions.text: What causes the daytime sky to look blue?
questions.fun_fact: Rayleigh scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength, so blue light scatters far more than red.

questions.text: What kind of energy does a moving object have because of its motion?
questions.fun_fact: Doubling an object's speed makes its kinetic energy four times greater, because it depends on the square of the speed.

questions.text: How does heat from the Sun reach Earth across empty space?
questions.fun_fact: At everyday temperatures, most thermal radiation is infrared, which thermal cameras can detect.

questions.text: A bimetallic strip bends when heated because its two bonded metals do what?
questions.fun_fact: Clockmaker John Harrison invented the bimetallic strip around 1759 for a marine chronometer.

questions.text: Which phenomenon makes waves spread out as they pass through a narrow opening?
questions.fun_fact: Italian scientist Francesco Grimaldi studied it in the 1600s and coined the word diffraction.

questions.text: The 1798 Cavendish experiment, which used a torsion balance, is often described as weighing what?
questions.fun_fact: Cavendish found the Earth to be about 5.4 times denser than water, close to the modern value.

questions.text: Which Italian physicist led the team that built the first nuclear reactor, Chicago Pile-1, in 1942?
questions.fun_fact: The reactor was built beneath the stands of a University of Chicago stadium using uranium and graphite.

questions.text: Which SI unit measures inductance?
questions.fun_fact: It is named after Joseph Henry, who discovered electromagnetic induction independently of Michael Faraday at about the same time.

questions.text: Which SI prefix stands for 10⁻⁹, one billionth?
questions.fun_fact: The prefix comes from the Greek word for dwarf.

questions.text: Which particle, announced at CERN in 2012, is linked to the field that gives other particles their mass?
questions.fun_fact: François Englert and Peter Higgs shared the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics for predicting it.

questions.text: What is the SI base unit of mass?
questions.fun_fact: Until 2019 it was defined by a platinum-iridium cylinder kept near Paris; it is now defined using fixed values of physical constants.

questions.text: Why does water boil at a lower temperature on a high mountain?
questions.fun_fact: At 1,905 m above sea level, water boils at about 93.4 °C instead of 100 °C.

questions.text: A step-down transformer, like the one in a phone charger, lowers which electrical quantity?
questions.fun_fact: Since the 1880s, transformers have been essential for the transmission and distribution of alternating-current power.

questions.text: GPS satellite clocks must be corrected for time effects predicted by which theory?
questions.fun_fact: Relativity makes GPS satellite clocks run about 38 microseconds per day faster than clocks on the ground; the system corrects for it.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.fun_fact: It is named after James Watt, the Scottish engineer who improved the Newcomen steam engine in 1776.

questions.text: Which SI unit measures electrical capacitance?
questions.fun_fact: A farad is so large that practical capacitors are usually rated in microfarads or even smaller units.

questions.text: About how fast does sound travel through air at 20 °C?
questions.fun_fact: In fresh water, sound travels at roughly 1,480 m/s, more than four times faster than in air.

questions.text: Which German physicist coined the term entropy in 1865?
questions.fun_fact: He built the word from the Greek for transformation, to echo the word energy.

questions.text: What is the blue glow seen in the water around some nuclear reactor cores called?
questions.fun_fact: Pavel Cherenkov shared the 1958 Nobel Prize in Physics with Ilya Frank and Igor Tamm.

questions.text: Which SI unit measures electric current?
questions.fun_fact: It is named after André-Marie Ampère, considered the father of electromagnetism along with Hans Christian Ørsted.

questions.text: What is the bending of light as it passes from air into water called?
questions.fun_fact: The amount of bending is given by Snell's law, which links the angles of the light to its speed in each material.

questions.text: In the acronym LASER, what does the S stand for?
questions.fun_fact: Gordon Gould first published the acronym LASER in a 1959 conference paper.

questions.text: Which Japanese physicist predicted the existence of the meson in 1935?
questions.fun_fact: He received the 1949 Nobel Prize in Physics after the pi meson he predicted was discovered in 1947.

questions.text: Sound travels through air as which kind of wave?
questions.fun_fact: In solids, sound can also travel as transverse waves, which liquids and gases cannot carry.

questions.text: Astronauts float aboard the International Space Station because they are in a constant state of what?
questions.fun_fact: Calling it zero gravity is misleading: at the Station's altitude, gravity is only slightly weaker than on the ground.

questions.text: What is the temperature called above which a material loses its permanent magnetism?
questions.fun_fact: It is named after Pierre Curie, who showed that magnetism is lost at a critical temperature.

questions.text: Which English scientist discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831?
questions.fun_fact: Faraday had little formal schooling and began his working life as a bookbinder's apprentice.

questions.text: In the formula V = IR from Ohm's law, what does R stand for?
questions.fun_fact: Georg Ohm published his law in 1827, after experiments with wires of different lengths.

questions.text: Protons and neutrons are made of smaller particles called what?
questions.fun_fact: Murray Gell-Mann took the name quark from a line in James Joyce's novel Finnegans Wake.

questions.text: Which effect makes a spinning ball curve away from the path it would follow without spin?
questions.fun_fact: In baseball, it gives a curveball with topspin its sharp downward swerve.

questions.text: Which French engineer wrote the 1824 work Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire?
questions.fun_fact: It was his only publication, and it developed the first successful theory of the maximum efficiency of heat engines.

questions.text: Which English polymath's double-slit experiment around 1801 supported the wave theory of light?
questions.fun_fact: Young also helped decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs using the Rosetta Stone.

questions.text: The word electricity comes from the Greek word for which material?
questions.fun_fact: William Gilbert coined the Latin word electricus, meaning of amber, in 1600 after studying rubbed amber.

questions.text: Which common liquid takes a lot of energy to warm up, helping oceans moderate coastal temperatures?
questions.fun_fact: Raising 1 kg of liquid water by 1 K takes about 4,184 J, one of the highest specific heats among common substances.

questions.text: Which nearly massless, uncharged particles stream from the Sun in vast numbers and rarely interact with matter?
questions.fun_fact: Solar neutrinos originate from the nuclear fusion that powers the Sun.

questions.text: After two half-lives, what fraction of a radioactive sample's original atoms remains?
questions.fun_fact: Ernest Rutherford discovered the principle in 1907; the original term, half-life period, was shortened to half-life in the 1950s.

questions.text: Which SI unit counts one radioactive decay per second?
questions.fun_fact: The older unit, the curie, equals 37 billion becquerels.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.fun_fact: Weather reports usually give air pressure in hectopascals; typical sea-level pressure is about 1,013 hPa.

questions.text: What is the process of splitting a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter ones called?
questions.fun_fact: Physicist Otto Frisch named the process fission by analogy with the division of living cells.

questions.text: Which French physicist showed in the 1780s that the force between electric charges falls with the square of their distance?
questions.fun_fact: He is one of the 72 French scientists whose names are inscribed on the Eiffel Tower.

questions.text: In a primary rainbow, which color appears on the outer edge of the arc?
questions.fun_fact: In a primary rainbow the most intense light returns at 42 degrees, an angle that does not depend on raindrop size.

questions.text: Which subatomic particle in an atom has no electric charge?
questions.fun_fact: A free neutron outside a nucleus decays with a mean lifetime of roughly 15 minutes.

questions.text: Which is the SI base unit of temperature?
questions.fun_fact: Since 2019 the kelvin has been defined by fixing the exact numerical value of the Boltzmann constant.

questions.text: What is the SI base unit of time?
questions.fun_fact: Dividing a day into 24 hours of 60 minutes, each of 60 seconds, gives 86,400 seconds per day.

questions.text: Which Danish physicist proposed in 1913 that electrons orbit the nucleus at fixed energy levels?
questions.fun_fact: He received the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on the structure of atoms.

questions.text: According to Newton's third law, every action has an equal and opposite what?
questions.fun_fact: Rockets rely on it: they push exhaust gas backward, and the gas pushes the rocket forward.

questions.text: Which Austrian physicist discovered cosmic rays on high-altitude balloon flights in 1912?
questions.fun_fact: He shared the 1936 Nobel Prize in Physics for this discovery.

questions.text: What is the steady maximum speed of a falling object called, reached when air drag balances its weight?
questions.fun_fact: A skydiver falling belly-down has a terminal speed of about 55 m/s, roughly 200 km/h.

questions.text: What are materials called whose electrical resistance drops to exactly zero below a critical temperature?
questions.fun_fact: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes discovered superconductivity in 1911 while cooling mercury.

questions.text: Which kind of material, such as copper, lets electric current flow through it easily?
questions.fun_fact: Metals conduct well because they have a delocalized sea of electrons that can move easily through the material.

questions.text: What does a Geiger counter detect?
questions.fun_fact: Hans Geiger and Ernest Rutherford built an early version in 1908; the Geiger-Müller tube followed in 1928.

questions.text: The meter is defined using which fundamental constant?
questions.fun_fact: Since 1983 the meter has been the distance light travels in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second.

questions.text: Which type of radiation consists of helium nuclei ejected from radioactive atoms?
questions.fun_fact: Alpha particles penetrate very little: a few centimeters of air, or the outer layer of skin, stops them.

questions.text: Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for explaining which effect?
questions.fun_fact: Einstein was born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg, in 1879 and grew up in Munich.

questions.text: Which German physicist formulated the uncertainty principle in 1927?
questions.fun_fact: He won the 1932 Nobel Prize in Physics for the creation of quantum mechanics.

questions.text: Which quantum effect lets particles cross an energy barrier they classically lack the energy to pass?
questions.fun_fact: George Gamow used tunneling in 1928 to explain alpha decay.

questions.text: Which French physicist proposed in 1924 that electrons and other matter have wave properties?
questions.fun_fact: He came from a noble family and later held the title of duc de Broglie.

questions.text: Which Pakistani physicist shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on electroweak unification?
questions.fun_fact: In 1964 he founded the International Centre for Theoretical Physics in Trieste, Italy.

questions.text: Which law states that, at constant temperature, a gas's pressure falls as its volume rises?
questions.fun_fact: French physicist Edme Mariotte found the same law independently, so it is also called Mariotte's law.

questions.text: Which American physicist's 1923 discovery of wavelength shifts in scattered X-rays demonstrated the particle nature of light?
questions.fun_fact: He shared the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics with C. T. R. Wilson.

questions.text: Which Dutch scientist set out a wave theory of light in his 1690 Treatise on Light?
questions.fun_fact: He was also the first to explain Saturn's odd appearance as a thin, flat ring that touches the planet nowhere.

questions.text: Which astronomer discovered infrared radiation in 1800 by measuring temperatures beyond red light?
questions.fun_fact: He called the invisible heat rays calorific rays.

questions.text: What is absolute zero on the Celsius scale?
questions.fun_fact: The third law of thermodynamics says no process can cool a system all the way down to absolute zero in a finite number of steps.

questions.text: Which of these can sound NOT travel through?
questions.fun_fact: In iron, sound travels at about 5,120 m/s, almost 15 times faster than in air.

questions.text: Which law says a spring stretches in proportion to the force pulling it, up to a limit?
questions.fun_fact: Robert Hooke first published it in 1676 as a Latin anagram, ceiiinosssttuv.

questions.text: Which SI base unit measures luminous intensity?
questions.fun_fact: Its name comes from the Latin word for candle, and early standards were based on real candle flames.

questions.text: Which Chinese-American physicist's 1950s experiment showed that parity is not conserved in weak interactions?
questions.fun_fact: In 1978 she became the first winner of the Wolf Prize in Physics.

questions.text: Which Italian inventor shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics for wireless telegraphy?
questions.fun_fact: He shared the prize with German physicist Karl Ferdinand Braun.

questions.text: Which particle accelerator, invented by Ernest Lawrence around 1930, sends particles around in a spiral?
questions.fun_fact: It was the first cyclical accelerator, and it earned Lawrence the 1939 Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.text: Which Indian physicist's work on photon statistics led to particles being named bosons?
questions.fun_fact: Bose sent his paper to Einstein in 1924, who translated it into German and arranged its publication.

questions.text: Which principle says two identical fermions cannot occupy the same quantum state?
questions.fun_fact: Wolfgang Pauli formulated it in 1925 for electrons; his 1940 spin-statistics theorem extended it to all fermions.

questions.text: When white light passes through a glass prism, which color bends the most?
questions.fun_fact: For most glasses the refractive index is higher for blue light than for red, so a prism spreads white light into a spectrum.

questions.text: Which invisible light, just beyond violet, makes certain materials glow under a black light?
questions.fun_fact: German physicist Johann Ritter discovered it in 1801 by watching silver chloride darken beyond the violet end of the spectrum.

questions.text: What do you get when electric current flows through a coil of wire wound around an iron core?
questions.fun_fact: English inventor William Sturgeon demonstrated the first electromagnet in 1824.

questions.text: Which law of thermodynamics defines temperature through thermal equilibrium?
questions.fun_fact: Ralph H. Fowler established it in the 1930s, long after the other three laws were widely recognized.

questions.text: Which particle is the quantum of light?
questions.fun_fact: Chemist Gilbert N. Lewis popularized the word photon in 1926.

questions.text: According to Einstein, how does a clock moving close to the speed of light tick compared with a stationary observer's clock?
questions.fun_fact: A cosmic-ray muon traveling at 98% of the speed of light lives about five times longer than a muon at rest.

questions.text: Which property of a sound wave determines how high or low its pitch is?
questions.fun_fact: The human ear is sensitive to frequencies from about 20 Hz to about 20,000 Hz.

questions.text: Which value is closest to the acceleration of free fall at Earth's surface?
questions.fun_fact: Standard gravity is defined as exactly 9.80665 m/s², a value fixed by international agreement.

questions.text: Which number gives an object's speed as a ratio to the local speed of sound?
questions.fun_fact: The speed of sound depends on air temperature, so the same airspeed can give different Mach numbers at different altitudes.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.fun_fact: One joule is the work done when a force of one newton moves an object one meter in the direction of the force.

questions.text: Which American physicist's oil-drop experiment measured the charge of a single electron?
questions.fun_fact: He won the 1923 Nobel Prize in Physics and later chaired the executive council of Caltech.

questions.text: What is the antiparticle of the electron called?
questions.fun_fact: Carl Anderson spotted the first positron in cosmic-ray tracks in 1932.

questions.text: Mass multiplied by velocity gives which quantity?
questions.fun_fact: Newton's second law says the net force on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum.

questions.text: Which property describes an object's tendency to keep its state of motion unless a force acts on it?
questions.fun_fact: Isaac Newton described inertia in his first law of motion, which is also called the principle of inertia.

questions.text: The 1887 Michelson-Morley experiment failed to detect what?
questions.fun_fact: Albert Michelson became the first American to win a Nobel Prize in the sciences, in 1907.

questions.text: Total internal reflection traps light inside which data-carrying technology?
questions.fun_fact: Charles Kao shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on carrying light through fibers for communication.

questions.text: Which quantum phenomenon did Einstein call spooky action at a distance?
questions.fun_fact: Alain Aspect, John Clauser and Anton Zeilinger won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics for entanglement experiments.

questions.text: Which force resists the sliding of two surfaces against each other?
questions.fun_fact: Friction turns motion energy into thermal energy, which is why your hands warm up when you rub them together.

questions.text: Which machine converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
questions.fun_fact: A generator and an electric motor work on the same principle, but in opposite directions.

questions.text: Which planet is home to Olympus Mons, a giant shield volcano about 21 km high?
questions.fun_fact: Its base is about 600 km wide, and a cliff up to 8 km tall rings much of its outer edge.

questions.text: Which compound in its dust and rocks gives Mars its reddish color?
questions.fun_fact: The Martian surface can look like butterscotch, and fine iron oxide dust covers much of it.

questions.text: Which is the second-largest planet in the Solar System?
questions.fun_fact: Saturn's largest moon, Titan, is bigger than the planet Mercury, though less massive.

questions.text: Which is the only planet in the Solar System not named after a Greek or Roman god?
questions.fun_fact: Earth comes from Old English eorðe, a word with cognates in every Germanic language.

questions.text: Which element makes up most of the Sun's mass?
questions.fun_fact: The Sun's outer layer is about 73 percent hydrogen and 25 percent helium by mass.

questions.text: Which process in its core releases the energy that makes the Sun shine?
questions.fun_fact: The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago, and hydrogen-to-helium fusion has powered it since.

questions.text: What name is given to the stream of charged particles that flows constantly outward from the Sun?
questions.fun_fact: The solar wind inflates the heliosphere, a huge bubble that surrounds the Sun and its planets.

questions.text: Which W-shaped constellation is named after a mythical queen?
questions.fun_fact: In myth she was condemned to wheel around the north celestial pole on her throne.

questions.text: Why do stars appear to twinkle when seen from the ground?
questions.fun_fact: Planets usually twinkle less than stars because they look like tiny discs rather than single points of light.

questions.text: Light from far-off galaxies that are moving away from us is shifted toward which color?
questions.fun_fact: Gravity can redshift light too, as radiation climbs out of a gravitational well.

questions.text: Which of the eight planets orbits farthest from the Sun?
questions.fun_fact: Neptune orbits about 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth does.

questions.text: Which dog became the first animal to orbit Earth, aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957?
questions.fun_fact: Soviet scientists picked Moscow strays, assuming they were already used to cold and hunger.

questions.text: Jupiter is named after the Roman god holding which role?
questions.fun_fact: Jupiter holds about 2.5 times the mass of all the other planets combined.

questions.text: What is a huge system of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity called?
questions.fun_fact: Galaxies range from dwarfs with under a thousand stars to giants with a hundred trillion.

questions.text: The faint, hazy band of light across a dark night sky is our view of what?
questions.fun_fact: The band is the glow of countless stars in the Milky Way's disk, too far away to be seen one by one.

questions.text: Which informal English name is often used for astronauts from China?
questions.fun_fact: The word taikonaut is built from the Chinese word taikong, meaning outer space.

questions.text: About what fraction of Earth's gravity would you feel standing on the Moon?
questions.fun_fact: The Moon's surface gravity is also about half that of Mars.

questions.text: What do we call the changing shapes of the Moon's lit side over the month?
questions.fun_fact: The Moon's phases happen because we see different amounts of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth.

questions.text: Which zodiac constellation is named for a lion?
questions.fun_fact: Babylonian astronomers called its bright star Regulus the star that stands at the lion's breast.

questions.text: Which color of star is the hottest?
questions.fun_fact: Stars are classed by the letters O, B, A, F, G, K and M, from hottest to coolest. The Sun is a G star.

questions.text: Which two planets orbit closer to the Sun than Earth does?
questions.fun_fact: The four rocky inner planets have few or no moons and no ring systems.

questions.text: Which is the largest of the four rocky planets of the inner Solar System?
questions.fun_fact: Earth is also the densest planet in the Solar System.

questions.text: A comet's solid nucleus is often described as a dirty what?
questions.fun_fact: After NASA's Deep Impact probe hit comet Tempel 1 in 2005, many astronomers began preferring the term icy dirtballs.

questions.text: How did Apollo crews return to Earth at the end of their missions?
questions.fun_fact: On early Mercury flights a helicopter lifted the capsule from the water and carried it to a nearby ship.

questions.text: Which planet lies between Saturn and Neptune?
questions.fun_fact: Uranus is just visible to the naked eye, but it is so dim and slow that ancient observers never saw it as a planet.

questions.text: In which direction does Earth rotate?
questions.fun_fact: Seen from above Polaris, Earth turns counterclockwise.

questions.text: What are Saturn's rings made of, mostly?
questions.fun_fact: The ring particles range from micrometers to meters in size.

questions.text: Under the definition the IAU adopted in 2006, how many planets does the Solar System have?
questions.fun_fact: After the Sun, the eight planets are the most massive objects in the Solar System.

questions.text: Which planet lies between Earth and Jupiter?
questions.fun_fact: Mars is about half as wide as Earth and twice as wide as the Moon.

questions.text: Which planet has an average density lower than that of water?
questions.fun_fact: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 grams per cubic centimeter, lower than water's 1.0.

questions.text: In 1781, William Herschel discovered which planet?
questions.fun_fact: Herschel first proposed naming it Georgium Sidus, Latin for George's Star, after King George III.

questions.text: Which moon of Jupiter is the most volcanically active world in the Solar System?
questions.fun_fact: Io has over 400 active volcanoes, and tidal heating from Jupiter drives them.

questions.text: Which pair of NASA rovers landed on Mars in January 2004?
questions.fun_fact: Both rovers far outlived their planned missions of 90 Martian days; Opportunity worked until June 2018.

questions.text: Which NASA spacecraft became the first to orbit Jupiter, arriving in 1995?
questions.fun_fact: In 2003 Galileo was deliberately sent into Jupiter's atmosphere to avoid contaminating moons such as Europa.

questions.text: Which comet's fragments struck Jupiter in July 1994, the first direct observation of a collision between Solar System bodies?
questions.fun_fact: The comet had broken apart in July 1992, two years before its fragments hit Jupiter.

questions.text: What is the ring of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit, home to Pluto, called?
questions.fun_fact: The first Kuiper belt object found since Pluto, 15760 Albion, was discovered in 1992.

questions.text: Which is Pluto's largest moon, so big that the two orbit a point in space between them?
questions.fun_fact: Christy noticed that Pluto's image looked periodically elongated on photographic plates; the bulge was Charon.

questions.text: Which gas in their atmospheres gives Uranus and Neptune their blue tint?
questions.fun_fact: Voyager 2's 1989 images exaggerated Neptune's colors, creating the myth that it is a deep azure blue.

questions.text: Which planet has the shortest day, spinning once in about ten hours?
questions.fun_fact: Its fast spin makes Jupiter an oblate spheroid, about 7 percent wider at the equator than at the poles.

questions.text: What is the name for the dark, flat plains on the Moon, from a Latin word for seas?
questions.fun_fact: The maria are ancient basalt lava flows that filled huge impact basins.

questions.text: What gives a totally eclipsed Moon its reddish glow?
questions.fun_fact: It is the same effect that turns the sky red at sunset and sunrise.

questions.text: What is a solar eclipse called when the Moon is too far away to cover the Sun and leaves a bright ring?
questions.fun_fact: In a total eclipse, by contrast, the Moon fully covers the Sun's disk.

questions.text: What will the Sun become after it sheds its outer layers as a red giant?
questions.fun_fact: Its white dwarf will keep about 54 percent of the Sun's present mass.

questions.text: What is the Sun's visible surface layer called?
questions.fun_fact: Its effective temperature is about 5,772 kelvin, roughly 5,500 degrees Celsius.

questions.text: About how many years does the Sun's cycle of sunspot activity last?
questions.fun_fact: The cycle, also called the Schwabe cycle, was not clearly identified until 1843.

questions.text: Which type of star is the most common in the Milky Way?
questions.fun_fact: Red dwarfs burn their fuel so slowly that they can shine for trillions of years.

questions.text: What is the incredibly dense core left after a massive star explodes, about 20 km across, called?
questions.fun_fact: A typical neutron star packs about 1.4 solar masses into a radius of roughly 10 km.

questions.text: How many stars make up the Alpha Centauri system?
questions.fun_fact: Its two bright stars, Alpha Centauri A and B, orbit each other every 79 years or so.

questions.text: The astronomical unit was originally based on the average distance between Earth and what?
questions.fun_fact: In 2012 the IAU fixed the AU at exactly 149,597,870,700 meters.

questions.text: What is the shape of the Milky Way galaxy?
questions.fun_fact: Its disk is estimated to be about 87,000 light-years across.

questions.text: The Large and Small Magellanic Clouds are best seen from which part of the world?
questions.fun_fact: Both are dwarf galaxies that orbit the Milky Way.

questions.text: Which mysterious component is thought to drive the accelerating expansion of the universe?
questions.fun_fact: The first direct evidence came in 1998 from observations of distant Type Ia supernovae.

questions.text: About how old is the universe?
questions.fun_fact: One method matches the Lambda-CDM model to early-universe features such as the cosmic microwave background.

questions.text: Which supermassive black hole sits at the center of the Milky Way?
questions.fun_fact: The Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of Sagittarius A* in 2022.

questions.text: Whose observations of how galaxies rotate gave strong evidence for dark matter?
questions.fun_fact: A major observatory in Chile now bears Rubin's name.

questions.text: Vega is the brightest star in which northern constellation?
questions.fun_fact: Vega was the first star other than the Sun to have its image and spectrum photographed.

questions.text: India's first Mars probe, which entered Mars orbit in 2014, is unofficially known by what name?
questions.fun_fact: It made India the first Asian nation to reach orbit around Mars.

questions.text: The Southern African Large Telescope stands near the town of Sutherland in which country?
questions.fun_fact: Its main mirror is made of 91 hexagonal segments, each about 1 meter across.

questions.text: Charles Messier compiled his famous catalog of deep-sky objects to avoid mistaking them for what?
questions.fun_fact: A preliminary version of the catalog first appeared in 1774; it now lists 110 objects.

questions.text: Which astronomer formulated the equation in 1961 for estimating how many civilizations in our galaxy might be able to communicate?
questions.fun_fact: Drake formulated it to stimulate discussion at the first scientific meeting on SETI, not to give an exact count.

questions.text: Which British physicist wrote the 1988 bestseller A Brief History of Time?
questions.fun_fact: The book has sold more than 25 million copies and has been translated into dozens of languages.

questions.text: Arecibo Observatory, famed for its giant radio dish, is in which US territory?
questions.fun_fact: The 305-meter dish was built into a natural sinkhole.

questions.text: Jodrell Bank Observatory, home of the Lovell Telescope, is in which country?
questions.fun_fact: The telescope was the only one able to track Sputnik 1's booster rocket by radar, in 1957.

questions.text: Which instrument splits starlight into a spectrum so astronomers can tell what a star is made of?
questions.fun_fact: In the early 1800s Joseph von Fraunhofer used very pure prisms to see 574 dark lines in a spectrum of sunlight.

questions.text: What name is given to the zone around a star where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface?
questions.fun_fact: It is often called the Goldilocks zone, because conditions there are neither too hot nor too cold.

questions.text: Which was the first satellite launched by the United States, in 1958?
questions.fun_fact: Its instruments discovered the Van Allen radiation belts around Earth.

questions.text: Who became the first American to orbit Earth, in February 1962?
questions.fun_fact: Glenn flew in space again in 1998, at age 77, aboard the Space Shuttle.

questions.text: In which part of the Moon did the Apollo 11 lunar module land in July 1969?
questions.fun_fact: It contains Tranquility Base, the first place on another world visited by humans.

questions.text: Who stayed in lunar orbit aboard the Apollo 11 command module while Armstrong and Aldrin landed?
questions.fun_fact: Collins was also the first person to make more than one spacewalk, on Gemini 10 in 1966.

questions.text: Which rocket carried Apollo astronauts toward the Moon?
questions.fun_fact: The Saturn V's first stage produced about 34.5 meganewtons of thrust at launch.

questions.text: Where is the National Baseball Hall of Fame located?
questions.fun_fact: The museum was dedicated in 1939, three years after the first group of inductees was chosen.

questions.text: Which hockey legend is nicknamed "The Great One"?
questions.fun_fact: The NHL retired his number 99 for every team in 2000.

questions.text: What material are standard ice hockey pucks made of?
questions.fun_fact: Pucks are frozen before games to reduce bouncing.

questions.text: In 1869, Rutgers played which school in the first intercollegiate football game?
questions.fun_fact: The teams used improvised rules closer to soccer and rugby, and each school won its home game.

questions.text: Who broke Major League Baseball's color barrier in 1947 with the Brooklyn Dodgers?
questions.fun_fact: In 1997, MLB retired his number 42 across all teams.

questions.text: Which 1970s NHL team was nicknamed the "Broad Street Bullies"?
questions.fun_fact: Philadelphia won back-to-back Stanley Cups in 1974 and 1975.

questions.text: Which Giants outfielder made "The Catch" in Game 1 of the 1954 World Series?
questions.fun_fact: He caught Vic Wertz's deep fly ball on the warning track at the Polo Grounds.

questions.text: How many points does a safety score in American football?
questions.fun_fact: After a safety, the team that gave it up kicks the ball to the scoring team from its own 20-yard line.

questions.text: What does MLB's Gold Glove Award recognize?
questions.fun_fact: Rawlings has sponsored the award since it began in 1957.

questions.text: What song is traditionally sung during baseball's seventh-inning stretch?
options: Take Me Out to the Ball Game
questions.fun_fact: Jack Norworth was inspired to write the lyrics in 1908 by a subway sign advertising a Polo Grounds game.

questions.text: The Cy Young Award goes to the best player in which role?
questions.fun_fact: Introduced in 1956, it was first given to one pitcher in all of baseball, before each league got its own winner.

questions.text: Which team won the first Super Bowl, played in January 1967?
questions.fun_fact: The game, played at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, did not sell out.

questions.text: In which Massachusetts city is the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame?
questions.fun_fact: The hall inducted its first class in 1959 and opened its first facility in 1968.

questions.text: Which German star led the Dallas Mavericks to the 2011 NBA championship?
questions.fun_fact: He was named Finals MVP after the Mavericks beat the Miami Heat in six games.

questions.text: What is the area where baseball relief pitchers warm up called?
questions.fun_fact: In the late 1800s, "bullpen" meant a foul-territory area where latecomers to games were herded like cattle.

questions.text: Which trophy is awarded to the winner of the Super Bowl?
questions.fun_fact: Tiffany & Co. crafts a new sterling silver trophy for the champion each year.

questions.text: In baseball, what is it called when a batter hits the ball over the outfield fence in fair territory?
questions.fun_fact: On a home run, the batter and any runners already on base all score.

questions.text: How many players per team are on the court at once in basketball?
questions.fun_fact: The first official game, played in 1892 at an Albany YMCA, ended 1-0, with the only shot made from 25 feet (7.6 m).

questions.text: The NHL's Vezina Trophy goes to the league's best player in which position?
questions.fun_fact: It is named for Georges Vezina, a Montreal Canadiens goaltender, and was first awarded for the 1926-27 season.

questions.text: The Heisman Trophy honors the top player in which sport?
questions.fun_fact: It was renamed in 1936 for John Heisman, athletic director of the Downtown Athletic Club that created it.

questions.text: Which team's win in Super Bowl III shocked the heavily favored Baltimore Colts?
questions.fun_fact: Three days before the game, quarterback Joe Namath publicly guaranteed a Jets victory.

questions.text: How many seconds is the shot clock in NBA games?
questions.fun_fact: Syracuse Nationals owner Danny Biasone tested a 24-second shot clock in a scrimmage in 1954.

questions.text: Which team sold Babe Ruth to the Yankees, starting the "Curse of the Bambino"?
questions.fun_fact: The Red Sox drought lasted from 1918 until their World Series win in 2004.

questions.text: In ice hockey, where does a penalized player serve his time?
questions.fun_fact: A minor penalty sends a player off for two minutes, and no substitute is allowed to replace him.

questions.text: How high above the floor is a regulation basketball rim?
questions.fun_fact: The steel rim is 18 inches (46 cm) in diameter.

questions.text: Which Yale player and coach is known as the "Father of American Football"?
questions.fun_fact: Camp's rule changes introduced the line of scrimmage and the system of downs.

questions.text: How many points is a successful free throw worth in basketball?
questions.fun_fact: The free-throw line is informally known as the foul line or the "charity stripe".

questions.text: How many downs does an offense get to advance the ball 10 yards in American football?
questions.fun_fact: A team that fails to gain the 10 yards on fourth down usually punts or tries a field goal instead.

questions.text: What is the NCAA men's Division I basketball tournament popularly called?
questions.fun_fact: The tournament began in 1939 and is played as a single-elimination bracket.

questions.text: Who caught the winning touchdown pass known as "The Catch" in the January 1982 NFC Championship Game?
questions.fun_fact: The game was played at Candlestick Park, and the 49ers went on to win Super Bowl XVI.

questions.text: How long is an American football field between the two goal lines?
questions.fun_fact: Numbers are painted inside each sideline at 10-yard intervals, counting up to 50 at midfield.

questions.text: Which UCLA basketball coach was nicknamed "The Wizard of Westwood"?
questions.fun_fact: He led UCLA to ten NCAA championships in twelve seasons, from 1964 to 1975.

questions.text: Which rival league, founded in 1959, merged with the NFL?
questions.fun_fact: The merger took full effect in 1970, when the AFL's teams became part of the NFL.

questions.text: Bevo, a live Longhorn steer, is the mascot of which university's teams?
questions.fun_fact: The first Bevo appeared at Texas's 1916 Thanksgiving Day game.

questions.text: Which baseball park is famous for the ivy covering its outfield walls?
questions.fun_fact: Bill Veeck planted the ivy in 1937, inspired by the ivy at an Indianapolis ballpark.

questions.text: What office did Lord Stanley hold when he donated the Stanley Cup in 1892?
questions.fun_fact: The original silver bowl cost ten guineas.

questions.text: Which NFL team first raised money by selling 1,000 shares of stock to its local community in 1923?
questions.fun_fact: The Packers were founded in 1919, a year before the league that became the NFL.

questions.text: Michael Jordan won six NBA championships with which team?
questions.fun_fact: In between his two stretches with the Bulls, Jordan played minor league baseball in 1994 for the Birmingham Barons.

questions.text: Which Nigerian-born center, nicknamed "The Dream", led the Houston Rockets to the 1994 NBA title?
questions.fun_fact: He was the first pick of the 1984 draft, which also produced Michael Jordan, Charles Barkley and John Stockton.

questions.text: Which Hall of Fame center was famous for the "sky hook" shot?
questions.fun_fact: Born Ferdinand Lewis Alcindor Jr., he adopted the name Kareem Abdul-Jabbar in 1971.

questions.text: The Hobey Baker Award goes to the top player in which college sport?
questions.fun_fact: The award is named for Hobey Baker, who played college hockey at Princeton University.

questions.text: Harvard's annual football rivalry with Yale is known by what simple name?
questions.fun_fact: The two schools first played each other in 1875.

questions.text: In which city is the Hockey Hall of Fame located?
questions.fun_fact: The hall was established in 1943 in Kingston, Ontario, and its first permanent building opened in Toronto in 1961.

questions.text: In which Canadian city was the National Hockey League founded in 1917?
questions.fun_fact: The league began play with four teams after the earlier National Hockey Association suspended operations.

questions.text: Which team did the Baltimore Colts beat in overtime in the 1958 NFL title game, the "Greatest Game Ever Played"?
questions.fun_fact: It was the first NFL game to be decided in sudden-death overtime.

questions.text: Which Montreal Canadiens star was nicknamed "The Rocket"?
questions.fun_fact: In 1944-45 he became the first NHL player to score 50 goals in a season, doing it in 50 games.

questions.text: How many outs end each half-inning in baseball?
questions.fun_fact: The visiting team bats in the top half of each inning, and the home team bats in the bottom half.

questions.text: Which Dallas Cowboys quarterback popularized the term "Hail Mary pass" after a 1975 playoff win?
questions.fun_fact: His game-winning touchdown pass against the Minnesota Vikings was caught by Drew Pearson.

questions.text: Larry Bird spent his entire NBA career with which team?
questions.fun_fact: Drafted in 1978, Bird waited a year before joining the Celtics in 1979.

questions.text: How far apart are the bases on a Major League Baseball diamond?
questions.fun_fact: The front of the pitching rubber is 60 feet 6 inches (18.4 m) from home plate.

questions.text: Which team won the 2016 World Series, ending a 108-year championship drought?
questions.fun_fact: Game 7 went ten innings and ended 8-7, the first extra-innings Game 7 since 1997.

questions.text: Which New York Giants player hit the 1951 "Shot Heard 'Round the World"?
questions.fun_fact: Thomson's three-run homer came in the ninth inning of the third and deciding playoff game.

questions.text: The NBA was formed in 1949 when the Basketball Association of America merged with which league?
questions.fun_fact: The BAA had played its first game in Toronto in 1946.

questions.text: What is the nickname of the tall left-field wall at Boston's Fenway Park?
questions.fun_fact: The wall was painted green in 1947; before that it was covered in advertisements.

questions.text: Which Pittsburgh Steelers running back made the 1972 "Immaculate Reception"?
questions.fun_fact: The play beat the Oakland Raiders in a 1972 playoff game at Three Rivers Stadium.

questions.text: Which Atlanta Braves slugger was nicknamed "Hammerin' Hank"?
questions.fun_fact: He began his pro career with the Indianapolis Clowns of the Negro leagues.

questions.text: What color flag does an NFL official throw to signal a penalty?
questions.fun_fact: Coaches throw a red flag to challenge an official's ruling.

questions.text: How long is each quarter in an NBA game?
questions.fun_fact: College men's games are split into two halves of 20 minutes instead of quarters.

questions.text: In 1966, which school's NCAA champions became the first to start five Black players in the title game?
questions.fun_fact: Coach Don Haskins's team beat top-ranked Kentucky, coached by Adolph Rupp, in the final.

questions.text: In baseball, the designated hitter bats in place of which player?
questions.fun_fact: The American League adopted the rule in 1973; the National League followed in 2022.

questions.text: Which Japanese outfielder was the AL Rookie of the Year and MVP in 2001 with the Seattle Mariners?
questions.fun_fact: Before joining the majors he starred for the Orix BlueWave in Japan.

questions.text: Which university's women's basketball team won eight NCAA titles under coach Pat Summitt?
questions.fun_fact: She also coached the US women's national team to the Olympic gold medal in 1984.

questions.text: The Iron Bowl is Alabama's annual football rivalry game against which school?
questions.fun_fact: The name reflects Birmingham, a leading iron and steel producer, where the game was long played.

questions.text: Which New York Yankees star was nicknamed "The Iron Horse"?
questions.fun_fact: Gehrig played 2,130 consecutive games, a streak that stood for 56 years.

questions.text: Which school did Jay Berwanger attend when he won the first Heisman Trophy in 1935?
questions.fun_fact: He was the first player ever drafted by the NFL, in 1936, but never played pro football because of a salary dispute.

questions.text: What nickname is given to the World Series?
questions.fun_fact: The series is played as a best-of-seven playoff.

questions.text: Which Montreal Canadiens goalie popularized the goalie mask by wearing one in a game in 1959?
questions.fun_fact: He played for the Canadiens from 1953 to 1963, a span in which they won six Stanley Cups.

questions.text: Which of these teams was one of the NHL's "Original Six"?
questions.fun_fact: The Original Six era lasted from 1942 until the league expanded in 1967.

questions.text: How many innings are in a regulation Major League Baseball game?
questions.fun_fact: If the score is tied after nine innings, extra innings are played until one team is ahead at the end of an inning.

questions.text: Which university's teams are known as the Fighting Irish?
questions.fun_fact: The school's mascot is a Leprechaun, and its fight song is the Notre Dame Victory March.

questions.text: Which Detroit Tigers star was known as "The Georgia Peach"?
questions.fun_fact: In the first Hall of Fame balloting, in 1936, he received the most votes: 222 of a possible 226.

questions.text: Magic Johnson's Michigan State won the 1979 NCAA title over Larry Bird's team from which school?
questions.fun_fact: The final game marked the beginning of the rivalry between Johnson and Bird.

questions.text: In the World Series, the American League champion plays the champion of which other league?
questions.fun_fact: No World Series was played in 1904 or in 1994.

questions.text: Which team became the first openly all-professional baseball club in 1869?
questions.fun_fact: The team won 57 games and lost none in 1869, counting only matches against association clubs.

questions.text: What is the name of the NFL's annual championship game?
questions.fun_fact: Roman numerals were first used for Super Bowl V and applied retroactively to the first four games.

questions.text: In baseball, which fielder crouches behind home plate?
questions.fun_fact: Catchers' protective gear has been nicknamed the "tools of ignorance".
